key_points: Legacy SQL stored procedures are migrated to a lakehouse environment with minimal changes.
A specific procedure processing daily orders is translated using Databricks' procedural SQL features.
Unity Catalog provides governance, while session-scoped temporary tables replace legacy constructs.
Databricks supports native cursors and transaction semantics with BEGIN ATOMIC.
Migration reduces effort by 50-75% and preserves SQL team maintenance capabilities.
items.summary: The article discusses the migration of legacy SQL stored procedures to a lakehouse environment with minimal code changes. It highlights a specific example of a procedure that processes daily orders, involving temporary tables, validation loops, and transaction handling. The migration was achieved by translating the SQL code rather than rewriting it, leveraging Databricks' support for procedural SQL features. Key points include the use of Unity Catalog for governance, the replacement of temporary tables with session-scoped CREATE TEMP TABLE, native cursor support in Databricks SQL, and the use of BEGIN ATOMIC for transaction semantics. The migration reduces effort by 50-75% and allows SQL teams to maintain their logic while integrating with modern data platforms.
items.title: SQL Procedures Migrated to Lakehouse with Minimal Changes

key_points: Researchers found that scarce target corpora can be reused 15–20 times in mixture pretraining.
Optimal repetition of target data depends on data size, compute budget, and model scale.
A repetition-aware scaling law was introduced to determine effective mixture configurations.
Generic data plays a regularizing role in mixture training, reducing overfitting risks.
items.summary: A study examines the trade-off between target data repetition and model performance in language model training. Researchers found that scarce target corpora can be reused 15–20 times, with optimal repetition depending on data size, compute budget, and model scale. They introduced a repetition-aware scaling law to determine effective mixture configurations for pretraining under data constraints. The work highlights the role of generic data in regularization and provides practical recommendations for data mixtures.
items.title: Study finds optimal repetition of target data in mixture pretraining

items.summary: Databricks Genie Agents allow users to create domain-specific AI assistants from a single prompt by leveraging trusted business context. The agents reason over structured data, documents, and files governed by Unity Catalog, addressing the issue of missing context that often leads to inaccurate responses. By focusing on a single use case, teams can test and trust agents more effectively, as the quality of the agent depends on the curated context provided. The process begins with a prompt that describes the desired outcome and points to relevant data sources, enabling the agent to draw from the right information. Genie Agents can handle both structured and unstructured data, ensuring answers are grounded in the correct sources. Testing with predefined benchmarks helps improve accuracy, and agents can be expanded over time as more data and knowledge are added. The success of these agents relies on the quality of the underlying data and systems, emphasizing the importance of governance and domain expertise.
items.title: Genie Agents Enable Domain-Specific AI from Single Prompt

key_points: A study analyzed 21,000 conversations from four LLMs to examine human-like behaviors.
Behaviors varied across models and user factors like conversation goals and user profiles.
Human evaluators found self-referential and relationship-building behaviors less appropriate from LLMs.
System prompts can control these behaviors, but require careful evaluation to avoid unintended effects.
items.summary: A study examines the prevalence and control of human-like behaviors in large language models (LLMs), analyzing 21,000 conversations from four models. Researchers found these behaviors vary across models and user factors, with human evaluators perceiving self-referential and relationship-building behaviors as less appropriate from LLMs. System prompts can influence these behaviors, though careful evaluation is needed to avoid unintended effects. The study recommends responsible LLM design and evaluation practices.
items.title: Study explores human-like behaviors in LLMs across models and user factors

key_points: Optimal memory dosing for AI agents varies by model capability, with stronger models benefiting from full guideline sets and weaker models from curated retrieval.
The study evaluated eight models across the capability spectrum, showing that saturated models show no measurable gain from additional memory.
Curated retrieval proved both accurate and cost-effective, with gpt-oss-120b achieving significant task completion improvements at minimal token cost.
Memory is distilled from an agent's past trajectories and injected at inference time without weight updates, enabling efficient and portable learning.
Prompt caching and efficient retrieval strategies are recommended to manage costs in production while maintaining performance gains.
items.summary: A study evaluates how different AI models benefit from agentic memory, finding that the optimal amount of memory varies by model tier. Stronger models with headroom perform best with full guideline sets, while weaker models benefit from curated, task-specific retrieval. Saturated models show no measurable gain. The research, conducted on eight models ranging from 30B to 745B parameters, highlights that memory is distilled from an agent's past trajectories and injected at inference time without weight updates. The study uses AppWorld, a benchmark with 585 multi-step tasks, to measure performance improvements in task and scenario goal completion. Curated retrieval proved both accurate and cost-effective, with gpt-oss-120b achieving +16.1pp task completion at only +5% token cost. The findings suggest that memory should be calibrated to the model's capabilities, with prompt caching and efficient retrieval strategies helping to manage costs in production.
items.title: Optimal Memory Dosing for AI Agents Varies by Model Capability

key_points: Multi-vector models retain one vector per token, preserving detailed token-level information for better retrieval.
These models are effective for visual document retrieval and complex queries with multiple requirements.
They can be loaded via the sentence-transformers library, supporting various checkpoint formats.
Indexing and scoring use MaxSim to align query and document tokens, enhancing retrieval quality.
The models maintain compatibility with existing infrastructure while improving retrieval performance.

items.summary: Multi-vector embedding models, such as those from LightOn, use late interaction to improve retrieval by preserving token-level information. Unlike dense models that compress text into a single vector, these models retain one vector per token, allowing for more precise matching. This approach is particularly effective for visual document retrieval and complex queries with multiple requirements. The models can be loaded via the sentence-transformers library, with support for various checkpoint formats. Indexing and scoring use MaxSim to align query and document tokens, enhancing retrieval quality without sacrificing speed.
items.title: Multi-Vector Embedding Models Enable Enhanced Retrieval with Late Interaction

items.summary: Google Research scientists demonstrate PhotoScan, a deep learning framework that estimates body composition from smartphone photos, achieving accuracy comparable to DXA scans in predicting insulin resistance. The research shows that integrating body composition data from smartphone images improves insulin resistance prediction, with AUROC scores nearly matching clinical DXA data. The findings suggest a promising path for accessible, non-invasive screening of metabolic risk.

key_points: PyTorch has integrated FP8 training optimizations for AMD Instinct GPUs into TorchAO and TorchTitan, enabling competitive performance out of the box.
FP8 training on Llama3-8B achieved a 13.4% throughput gain over BF16, with minimal memory impact.
Optimizations for MoE models like DeepSeek-V3 671B recovered 89% of FP8 overhead through kernel fusion and memory-efficient techniques.
The work includes native support for AMD's FP8 format, grouped GEMM for MoE, and a Triton fusion pipeline to reduce quantization overhead.
items.summary: PyTorch developers have integrated FP8 training optimizations for AMD Instinct GPUs into TorchAO and TorchTitan, improving performance on large models. These enhancements include native support for AMD's FP8 format, grouped GEMM for MoE architectures, and a Triton fusion pipeline to reduce quantization overhead. On Llama3-8B, FP8 training achieved a 13.4% throughput gain over BF16. For MoE models like DeepSeek-V3 671B, optimizations recovered 89% of the initial FP8 overhead through kernel fusion and memory-efficient techniques. The work, a collaboration between AMD and Meta, ensures FP8 training on AMD GPUs is now available out of the box for the PyTorch community.
items.title: PyTorch Enhances FP8 Training on AMD GPUs with Optimizations and MoE Support

key_points: IBM's DocLang is a new markup language designed to improve AI's understanding of documents by providing a structured, machine-native representation.
DocLang addresses the limitations of traditional document formats by encoding semantics, layout, and reading order in a standardized format.
The language is open and governed by the Linux Foundation, with support from existing tools like Docling and ABBYY's FineReader Engine.
IBM highlights benefits such as higher accuracy, reduced hallucination, and improved governance, which could make DocLang a valuable standard for AI workflows.
Adoption challenges include migration costs and ensuring the standard remains open, but IBM believes the benefits justify the effort.
items.summary: IBM researchers have introduced DocLang, a markup language designed to enhance AI's ability to understand and process documents. DocLang, a constrained dialect of XML, aims to reduce latency and inference costs by providing a clear structure for AI models to interpret document content. It addresses the limitations of existing formats like PDF and DOCX, which were not designed for machine understanding. By encoding semantics, layout, and reading order, DocLang offers a standardized representation that improves accuracy and consistency. The language is open and governed by the Linux Foundation, with support from tools like Docling and ABBYY's FineReader Engine. While challenges remain in adoption and implementation, IBM argues that DocLang's benefits, including reduced hallucination and improved governance, make it a valuable addition to AI workflows.
items.title: IBM Introduces DocLang to Improve AI Understanding of Documents

key_points: Google Research finds LLMs often fail to recall encoded facts rather than lacking them.
Knowledge profiling distinguishes between encoding and recall failures in factual errors.
WikiProfile benchmark shows 26–34% of facts cannot be directly recalled by top models like Gemini-3-Pro and GPT-5.
Thinking-optimized models improve recall for encoded but inaccessible facts, suggesting better utilization of existing knowledge may enhance factuality.
The study reframes the long-tail problem as a recall issue rather than a knowledge acquisition one.
items.summary: A study by Google Research scientists Nitay Calderon and Gal Yona reveals that large language models (LLMs) often fail to recall encoded facts rather than lacking them. The research introduces a framework called knowledge profiling, which distinguishes between encoding and recall failures. Using a benchmark called WikiProfile, the study evaluates 13 LLMs, finding that while most facts are encoded, recall remains a significant challenge. For models like Gemini-3-Pro and GPT-5, 26–34% of facts cannot be directly recalled, and even with thinking, 11–12% remain inaccessible. The study suggests that recall issues, not encoding gaps, are the primary cause of factual errors in frontier LLMs. It also highlights that rare facts are encoded but difficult to access, and thinking-optimized models show improved recall for these cases, indicating that better utilization of existing knowledge may be key to improving factuality.
items.title: LLMs Struggle with Recall, Not Missing Knowledge, Study Finds

key_points: CARE-X integrates generative and discriminative capabilities to support diverse radiology tasks with both free-text and structured outputs.
The model uses DAPO-based reinforcement learning to optimize clinical fidelity and includes auxiliary heads for classification and visual grounding.
Validation on Indian clinical data shows improved detection of rare ICU conditions and measurement-dependent findings like cardiomegaly.
A separate study using Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct with deterministic tools demonstrates enhanced diagnostic accuracy through direct computation for quantitative assessments.
While not a medical device, CARE-X's results suggest potential for future clinical applications in radiology workflows.

items.summary: CARE-X is a research model designed to address gaps in current radiology vision-language models by integrating generative and discriminative capabilities. It supports diverse clinical tasks through dual inference, providing both free-text generation and structured predictions with calibrated confidence scores. The model uses reinforcement learning with DAPO to optimize clinical fidelity and includes auxiliary heads for classification and visual grounding. Validation on Indian clinical data shows improved performance in detecting rare ICU conditions and measurement-dependent findings like cardiomegaly. A separate study using Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct with deterministic tools demonstrates that direct computation can enhance diagnostic accuracy for quantitative assessments. While CARE-X is not a medical device, its results highlight potential for future clinical applications in radiology workflows.
items.title: CARE-X Model Combines Generative and Discriminative Capabilities for Enhanced Chest X-ray Interpretation

key_points: IBM Research and collaborators developed GENCO, a unified AI solver for grid analysis, to address the complexity of modern power grids.
GENCO unifies three core grid tasks—power flow, optimal power flow, and state estimation—into a single model, improving speed and accuracy.
The tool was validated on real-world data from Hydro-Québec's transmission network, demonstrating its practical applicability.
The project includes the GridFM Development Framework, which enables reproducible and fair benchmarking of neural grid solvers.
The initiative emphasizes open collaboration among industry, academia, and government to advance AI-driven grid management.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: IBM Research and collaborators have developed GENCO, a unified AI solver for grid analysis, as part of the OpenGridFM project. The tool addresses the growing complexity of modern power grids by unifying three core tasks—power flow, optimal power flow, and state estimation—into a single model. GENCO significantly improves speed and accuracy compared to traditional methods, with performance gains up to 30 times faster for power flow and 85 times faster for optimal power flow. The project also includes the GridFM Development Framework, which enables reproducible and fair benchmarking of neural grid solvers. The model was validated on real-world data from Hydro-Québec's transmission network, demonstrating its practical applicability. The initiative emphasizes open collaboration among industry, academia, and government to advance AI-driven grid management.
items.title: IBM and collaborators develop unified AI solver for grid analysis

key_points: AWS is hosting the Trainium Frontier competition to explore optimal AI model designs on its purpose-built Trainium chips.
Participants must train language models from scratch, modifying architecture, optimizer, training loop, and optionally custom kernels.
The competition has two phases, with the final score combining training efficiency and inference performance.
The goal is to understand how different hardware constraints influence the efficient frontier of model design.
The competition offers prizes, including recognition at a NeurIPS event and publication opportunities with Annapurna Labs.
items.summary: AWS launches the Trainium Frontier competition, inviting researchers to design and train language models on its purpose-built AI chips. The competition challenges participants to optimize model architectures, training loops, and custom kernels to achieve the best performance within a fixed time and compute budget. The goal is to explore how different hardware constraints influence the efficient frontier of model design. Participants start with a 50M parameter baseline and can modify all aspects of the model, including the optimizer and training process. The competition has two phases: an initial 30-minute training period and a four-hour phase with distributed parallelism. The final score combines training efficiency and inference performance. The competition aims to advance hardware-native model design and offers prizes, including recognition at a NeurIPS event and publication opportunities.
items.title: AWS Trainium Frontier competition explores optimal AI model designs on purpose-built chips

key_points: GeoPT uses synthetic dynamics to teach AI models physics through particle interactions.
The system achieves faster performance and requires up to 60% less data than existing models.
GeoPT accurately simulates complex physical scenarios, including vehicle collisions and light behavior.
The technology could reduce the need for physical experiments in engineering design.
Researchers aim to expand the system to model more complex phenomena like weather patterns.
items.summary: Researchers at MIT's CSAIL and Tsinghua University have developed GeoPT, a new pre-training approach that allows AI models to simulate physical scenarios more efficiently. Unlike traditional methods that rely on numerical solvers, GeoPT uses synthetic dynamics to learn physics from 1.3 million particle interactions, enabling faster training and reduced data requirements. The system can predict how vehicles, robots, and everyday objects respond to forces like wind, water, and collisions, with results up to six times more accurate than existing models. GeoPT's ability to generalize across complex 3D shapes and physical phenomena could revolutionize engineering testing, reducing the need for physical experiments. The researchers believe their work represents a step toward creating physics foundation models, which could be used for tasks like simulating weather patterns or testing new materials.
items.title: GeoPT enables faster, more accurate physics simulations for engineering applications

key_points: TutorMoments evaluates how LLMs balance support and challenge in math tutoring sessions.
The framework uses real tutoring transcripts and teacher annotations to identify key decision points.
LLMs tend to over-help, giving too much support and rarely pushing students for deeper thinking.
Specifying the trade-off in prompts improves performance, but models still struggle to match human tutors' nuanced judgment.
The project aims to help build AI tutors that adapt to individual student needs.
items.summary: TutorMoments is a framework that assesses how well large language models (LLMs) can balance providing support and encouraging independent thinking during math tutoring. The system uses real tutoring transcripts from U.S. students in grades 2-7, annotated by experienced teachers, to identify key decision points where tutors must decide between scaffolding or pushing for rigor. LLMs are tested by taking over these sessions and simulating tutoring interactions. Results show models tend to over-help, giving too much support and rarely challenging students. While specifying the trade-off in prompts improves performance, LLMs still struggle to match human tutors' nuanced judgment. The project, developed by researchers, aims to help build AI tutors that adapt to individual student needs rather than doing the work for them. The dataset and code are released for open research.
items.title: TutorMoments evaluates AI tutors' ability to balance support and challenge in math sessions

items.summary: NIST researchers and collaborators demonstrated the transmission of entangled photons over 62 kilometers of noisy aerial fiber, a critical step toward building practical quantum networks. By employing real-time polarization stabilization techniques developed by Qunnect, the team achieved a 92.8% success rate in maintaining entanglement over 24 hours. While not breaking distance records, the study highlights the feasibility of quantum networking in real-world conditions. The findings suggest that quantum networks could one day enable secure communications, advanced scientific research, and powerful quantum computing applications.

items.summary: Shieldstral, a 3B open-weights multimodal safety classifier, outperforms models up to 7x its size by framing content moderation as a policy-adaptive question-answering task. Unlike traditional guardrail models, it accepts plain-language policies at inference time, unifying text and image safety evaluation without retraining. Released under Apache 2.0, it delivers calibrated safety scores across diverse benchmarks while running efficiently on a single 16GB NVIDIA GPU. The model processes requests by framing them as binary question-answering tasks, with three components: an instruction defining safety criteria, a yes/no question, and the content to evaluate. This approach allows policies to be adapted at deployment time without retraining, offering flexibility across text, image, and multimodal content. Shieldstral was trained on heterogeneous data sources, calibrated for strictness, and fine-tuned using LoRA and SLERP merging techniques. It is part of the Open Secure AI Alliance and is available for download under Apache 2.0.
items.title: Shieldstral: Policy-Adaptive Multimodal Safety Classifier Outperforms Larger Models

items.summary: Meta has significantly improved the efficiency of its Generative Ads Recommendation Model (GEM), doubling end-to-end training efficiency to 20–25% Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) while scaling training FLOPs 4x in 12 months. The company achieved this through a combination of compute and scaling efficiency innovations. Customized attention mechanisms, such as Jagged Flash Attention (JFA) and Generalized Dot-Product Attention (GDPA), were developed to handle the unique challenges of recommendation workloads, including jagged sequences and asymmetric attention patterns. Additionally, mixed ultra-low precision training, including MXFP8, was optimized to maintain model quality while improving performance. The approach also involved advanced parallelism strategies and network topology mapping to reduce communication overhead across thousands of GPUs. These efforts enabled Meta to achieve better GPU utilization and efficient scaling for its large-scale recommendation model.

Orchard-SWE achieves 69.7% on SWE-bench Verified using about 3 billion parameters, while Orchard-GUI scores 68.4% across web navigation benchmarks.

items.summary: The Orchard framework introduces an open-source solution for scalable agentic AI, designed to overcome infrastructure bottlenecks in research. It features Orchard Env, a Kubernetes-based environment service that supports multiple agent types and tasks without modification. The framework includes three domain-specific training recipes—Orchard-SWE, Orchard-GUI, and Orchard-Claw—demonstrating that small open-weight models can achieve strong results on complex tasks. Orchard-SWE reaches 69.7% on SWE-bench Verified using about 3 billion parameters, while Orchard-GUI achieves 68.4% across web navigation benchmarks. The project also provides training data and evaluation methods to aid the research community. By enabling training directly within real deployment harnesses, Orchard reduces the gap between research and practical application, allowing agents to be trained and evaluated in the same environments they will operate in.
items.title: Orchard framework enables scalable agentic AI with open-source tools

items.summary: The federal government plans to mandate a new water allocation scheme for the Colorado River, reducing water access for California, Arizona, and Nevada by up to 40% annually. This follows a decade of failed state negotiations over dwindling water supplies. The plan, set to take effect in October, aims to give states time to address the crisis but has drawn criticism from experts who warn it could delay meaningful solutions. The Colorado River, once thought to have ample water, now provides only 12 million acre-feet annually, far below the 15 million promised in 1922. The Central Arizona Project, a critical water source for Phoenix, faces potential shutdowns if water levels continue to decline, threatening Arizona's economy and population. Meanwhile, agricultural and industrial users pay less for water than residential users, exacerbating overuse. Climate change, marked by reduced snowfall and faster melting, is cited as a primary cause, though political and economic interests hinder urgent action.

items.summary: The Energy Commission of Malaysia revised NEM 3.0 guidelines for solar PV installations, covering residential and government premises. items.summary: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed an executive order on August 18 imposing legally binding requirements on data centers with peak demand over 25 MW. The order mandates compliance with energy affordability, transparency, workforce development, and environmental standards as conditions for permits, tax benefits, and utility regulation. It removes data centers from the PA Permit Fast Track Program and requires developers to document local approvals and meet clean energy targets. The initiative, part of the Governor’s Responsible Infrastructure Development (GRID) framework, aims to shift costs and risks to developers, prevent speculative projects, and ensure community engagement. The order also directs the Public Utility Commission to address data center curtailment and cost allocation during grid emergencies. While legislative efforts to codify GRID have stalled in the Senate, the executive action seeks to enforce strict guardrails on data center development.
items.title: Pennsylvania Governor Imposes Binding Requirements on Data Centers to Address Energy and Community Concerns

key_points: Pennsylvania requires data centers over 25 megawatts to secure their own power or face grid curtailments.

items.summary: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro has issued an executive order requiring large data centers to secure their own power resources or face potential grid curtailments during emergencies. The order aligns with a proposal by grid operator PJM Interconnection, which aims to prevent data centers from driving up power prices. Under the plan, data centers over 25 megawatts must either pay for their own energy capacity or risk being cut off during peak grid stress. The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission is tasked with implementing rules to ensure data centers cover costs associated with grid upgrades and emergency power auctions. The order also mandates that data centers increase their use of carbon-free energy sources over the next decade. While the policy does not block data centers from operating, it introduces preferential treatment for those complying with the new requirements.
items.title: Pennsylvania mandates data centers secure their own power to avoid grid cuts

items.summary: A study by Adrien Bilal, Noémie Pinardon-Touati, and Conor Walsh estimates that the aggregate sentience losses from biodiversity loss over the past half-century exceed human sentience gains from population growth by at least 10,000-fold. key_points: Lisa D. Cook, a Federal Reserve official, warns that persistent inflation remains a significant risk despite signs of economic stability.

The labor market shows stability with an unemployment rate of 4.2 percent, though challenges persist for new entrants and concerns about AI's impact on jobs.

items.summary: Federal Reserve official Lisa D. Cook warns that persistent inflation remains a significant risk despite signs of economic stability. She notes that the U.S. economy has not reached the 2 percent inflation target in over five years, with current annual inflation near its highest level since 2023. Cook attributes recent inflationary pressures to two unanticipated shocks: the Middle East conflict, which has driven up energy prices and may affect other goods, and increased capital expenditures tied to AI infrastructure, which has caused price increases for tech equipment and utilities. While the labor market shows stability with an unemployment rate of 4.2 percent, Cook acknowledges challenges for new entrants and concerns about AI's impact on jobs. She emphasizes that the Federal Reserve will continue to monitor data and is prepared to act if disinflation does not occur soon, reiterating her commitment to returning inflation to target. Cook also highlights that while inflation expectations remain anchored, the Fed must remain vigilant in its policy actions.
items.title: Federal Reserve Official Warns of Persistent Inflation Risks Despite Economic Stability

items.summary: At the third annual Financial Inclusion Conference, Federal Reserve Board Governor Bowman emphasized the importance of responsible innovation in expanding financial access. The Federal Reserve emphasized the need for clear regulatory guidance and flexibility for smaller banks, while also ensuring appropriate oversight for higher-risk AI applications. items.title: Federal Reserve Highlights Role of Responsible Innovation in Financial Inclusion

items.summary: The Freedom 250 Grand Prix, an IndyCar race on Washington, D.C.'s National Mall, is the first and potentially last event of its kind, celebrating the nation's 250th birthday. key_points: Investors sold stocks and bonds as government efforts to control borrowing costs faced limited success.

Analysts cited growing national debt, inflation, and increased demand for long-term borrowing as key factors driving up bond yields.
Rising yields are pushing up mortgage rates and other borrowing costs, affecting consumers and businesses.
items.summary: Investors sold stocks and bonds as government efforts to control borrowing costs faced limited success. The Treasury Department attempted to stabilize bond yields by buying back government debt, but yields rebounded. Carl Tannenbaum of Northern Trust cited three factors driving up bond yields: growing national debt, persistent inflation, and increased demand for long-term borrowing from tech companies building AI infrastructure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent argued the economy is strong and inflation is temporary, but investors remained skeptical. The bond-buying program, set to end after midterms, was deemed too small and short-term by analysts. Rising yields are pushing up mortgage rates and other borrowing costs, affecting consumers and businesses.
items.title: Treasury's bond-buying effort fails to stabilize rising yields

items.summary: Bedbugs, known for their nocturnal feeding habits, are increasingly prevalent and may spread antibiotic-resistant infections like MRSA, according to researchers. The pests, which hide in furniture and bedding, can cause anemia and other health issues if left unchecked. While they are not known to spread diseases efficiently, a 2023 experiment suggested they could transmit MRSA between feedings. Bedbugs have become more resistant to pesticides, leading to a resurgence in infestations, particularly in low-income housing. Experts recommend prevention measures such as inspecting secondhand items and avoiding placing luggage on beds. For existing infestations, professional extermination and methods like silica dust or heat treatment are advised, though these can be costly and labor-intensive.
items.title: Bedbugs pose health risks and infestation challenges

items.summary: Bushfires have destroyed over 10,000 hectares of Burundi's Ruvubu National Park, with park rangers struggling to contain the flames due to limited resources. The fires, which have increased in frequency since late July, are suspected to be set by poachers seeking firewood or grazing land. Park chief manager Marc Bakundintwari noted trails leading to Tanzania may be used by individuals to ignite fires. With only 45 staff managing a 50,800-hectare park, the fires have consumed one-fifth of the protected area. The park, established in 1980, is home to diverse wildlife including 44 mammal species, 425 bird species, and Nile crocodiles.
items.title: Bushfires destroy 10,000 hectares in Burundi's Ruvubu National Park

key_points: Researchers report the first decline in US obesity rates in over a decade, based on data from 2023.
GLP-1 agonist drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy have seen a significant increase in prescriptions, contributing to weight loss for many users.
Experts acknowledge the role of these medications and lifestyle changes post-pandemic in the observed decline, but caution that causality has not been definitively proven.
Predictions suggest obesity rates may rise again by 2035, highlighting the need for further research on the long-term impact of these drugs.
Both researchers agree that while the decline is promising, more data is needed to determine if it represents a sustainable trend.
items.summary: Researchers suggest the United States may be reaching a turning point in obesity rates, with the first decline in obesity prevalence in over 10 years observed in 2023. Benjamin Rader, an epidemiologist, noted that data from over 16 million adults indicated a decline, which he attributed partly to the increased use of GLP-1 agonist drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy. These medications, originally developed for diabetes, have led to significant weight loss for many users. However, Rader cautioned that there is no definitive proof of a causal relationship between the drugs and the overall decline. Peminda Cabandugama, an endocrinologist, acknowledged the role of these medications and post-pandemic lifestyle changes in the trend. Despite the decline, some researchers, including those at the Institute of Health Metrics and Evaluation, predict obesity rates could rise again by 2035. Both experts agree that while the data is promising, more research is needed to determine if the trend is sustainable and whether the decline will have lasting public health impacts.
items.title: US Obesity Rates Show First Decline in Over a Decade, Researchers Note

items.summary: India's ethanol blending program is facing scrutiny as it diverts subsidized rice from the food security system to ethanol distilleries at a 40% lower price. The government procures rice at a minimum support price (MSP) using taxpayer funds and sells it to ethanol producers at a significantly reduced rate, despite ethanol remaining costlier than petrol. The program has created a surplus ethanol capacity of 700 crore litres, but the cost of ethanol remains higher than crude oil, making the economic viability of the program uncertain.

key_points: A constraint-aware GPU allocator improved utilization and priority-weighted output by up to 33 percentage points and 105% compared to a FIFO scheduler.
The allocator reorders allocation decisions to prioritize jobs based on their value and resource needs, addressing the incompatibility between real-time and batch-like workloads.
Real-time demand is treated as a dynamic curve, allowing GPUs to be reclaimed during troughs for batch work, while maintaining availability during peaks.

items.summary: A constraint-aware GPU allocator improved utilization and priority-weighted output by up to 33 percentage points and 105%, respectively, compared to a FIFO scheduler on identical hardware and workloads. The improvement stemmed from reordering allocation decisions to prioritize jobs based on their value and resource needs. Real-time inference, which requires elastic allocation, and batch-like jobs, which need contiguous GPU blocks, were managed through a formal model that enforces constraints such as GPU exclusivity, demand ranges, and non-preemption. The allocator treated real-time demand as a dynamic curve rather than a fixed reservation, reclaiming idle GPUs for batch work during troughs. It also prioritized jobs across the scheduling horizon, avoiding the inefficiencies of FIFO, which left high-priority tasks waiting behind earlier arrivals. The system, which runs in 1 to 2 milliseconds on contended scenarios, demonstrated gains across five benchmark scenarios, with the strongest improvement in a training-heavy workload. The results highlight the importance of prioritizing value over simple occupancy metrics in GPU scheduling.
items.title: Constraint-aware GPU Allocator Boosts Utilization and Priority Output by 33 Percentage Points

Non-experts saw improved accuracy with AI assistance, largely due to deference to the system, while clinicians performed best without explanations. The research highlights the risks of overreliance on AI explanations, especially for less experienced users. The study suggests that explainable AI can lead to automation bias, where users follow incorrect AI recommendations. Researchers recommend approaches that encourage critical thinking rather than blind trust in AI outputs. The findings emphasize the need to tailor AI systems to user expertise to avoid errors and ensure effective healthcare outcomes.

key_points: IBM researchers are developing quantum algorithms to solve complex differential equations more efficiently than classical methods.
Quantum approaches map differential equations to linear systems, enabling exponential speedups through techniques like the HHL algorithm.
Recent work on RLC circuits demonstrates logarithmic runtime scaling with quantum algorithms, compared to linear scaling in classical simulations.
Challenges remain in solving turbulent regimes like those in Navier-Stokes equations, though progress is being made in simpler cases.
Future research directions include expanding quantum SPICE-like tools and exploring applications in materials science and epidemiology.
items.summary: IBM researchers led by Hari Krovi are investigating how quantum computing can offer significant speedups in solving complex differential equations. These equations, which describe phenomena ranging from fluid dynamics to financial modeling, are challenging for classical computers as systems grow in size and complexity. Krovi's team is developing quantum algorithms that map differential equations to linear systems, leveraging techniques like the HHL algorithm to achieve exponential speedups. Their work includes applications to differential algebraic equations (DAEs) in electrical circuits and integral differential equations with memory, showing potential for quantum advantage in areas like RLC circuit simulations. While current quantum methods can handle simple cases, challenges remain in solving turbulent regimes like those described by the Navier-Stokes equation. The team is also exploring future directions, including quantum SPICE-like tools and applications in materials science and epidemiology.
items.title: IBM Researchers Explore Quantum Computing's Potential in Solving Differential Equations

items.summary: Tuhin Chakrabarty and his team used the infini-gram tool to analyze AI-generated books and found they contain more rare expressions from existing literature compared to human-written works. Among top-selling self-published books on Amazon, those with substantial AI text had 43.2% of their text matching rare expressions from existing books, compared to 37.6% in books without AI detection. The overlap was even greater when compared to award-winning literature, with AI-heavy books showing 41.6% of text matching rare expressions. Chakrabarty's research highlights how AI models draw on distinctive language from training data, raising copyright concerns. The study also suggests that AI-generated texts may more heavily rely on unique phrasing from published works than human authors, challenging assumptions about originality in writing.
items.title: AI-generated books draw more from existing literature than human-written ones

key_points: The Science One Framework eliminates hallucinations in AI-generated research by building verifiable evidence chains during the research process.
The CoE Audit protocol measures the integrity of AI-generated papers against their code and evidence, revealing significant hallucination rates in existing systems.
The Science One Framework outperforms current systems on benchmark tasks while achieving zero phantom references and perfect score verification.
Strict verifiability does not compromise the framework's scientific capabilities, as it matches or exceeds human expert performance on multiple tasks.
The framework is presented as an experimental prototype, not a production-ready tool, with potential applications in future AI research systems.
items.summary: The Science One Framework, developed by Google Cloud researchers Rui Meng and Tomas Pfister, introduces a new verifiability system called Chain-of-Evidence (CoE) to address hallucinations in AI-generated scientific research. Current autonomous research systems often produce non-existent citations, misaligned code-text, and unverifiable results. The Science One Framework, which builds evidence chains during research, achieves zero phantom references and fully verifiable scores. It outperforms existing systems like Sakana AI's AI Scientist v2 and DeepScientist on benchmark tasks such as MLE-Bench and Parameter-Golf. The CoE Audit, an automated protocol, evaluates AI-generated papers against their code and evidence, revealing that baselines hallucinate up to 21% of references. The framework maintains method-code alignment and achieves state-of-the-art performance without compromising scientific rigor. The Science One Framework is presented as an experimental prototype, not a production-ready tool.
items.title: Science One Framework Achieves Zero Hallucinations in AI-Generated Research

key_points: ControlG uses a PID controller to allocate computational resources to different objectives during training, avoiding gradient conflicts.
The framework outperforms existing multitask methods on nine graph benchmarks, achieving average ranks of 1.4, 1.9, and 1.8 across three tasks.
ControlG provides interpretability by tracking how computational resources are allocated to each objective during training.
The method was developed by Amazon researchers and presented at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML).
items.summary: A new framework called ControlG addresses the challenge of training machine learning models to handle multiple objectives simultaneously in graph self-supervised learning. The method, inspired by industrial control systems, uses a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller to allocate computational resources to different objectives over time, rather than blending gradients at each step. This approach avoids conflicts between objectives and improves performance on various graph benchmarks. ControlG outperforms existing multitask methods across node classification, link prediction, and node clustering tasks, with notable gains on both homophilic and heterophilic graphs. The framework also provides interpretability, allowing users to track how computational resources are allocated during training. The work was developed by Amazon researchers and presented at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML).
items.title: ControlG framework improves multitask machine learning by coordinating objectives through PID control

key_points: EvoLib transforms raw experience into an evolving library of reusable knowledge.
The framework continuously refines and consolidates knowledge as new experiences arrive.
EvoLib outperforms existing memory approaches in diverse tasks with more efficient token usage.
The system maintains stable performance regardless of task order, showing robustness in real-world scenarios.
EvoLib enables AI systems to continually improve and adapt after deployment, similar to human learning.
items.summary: EvoLib is a framework that allows AI systems to learn from their experiences by transforming raw data into an evolving library of reusable knowledge. Unlike traditional memory systems that store static experiences, EvoLib continuously refines and consolidates knowledge as new experiences arrive. The framework extracts skills from successful solutions and insights from mistakes, making them more general and applicable across tasks. Key mechanisms include consolidation, which merges similar knowledge, and a weighting system that prioritizes knowledge based on its long-term utility. Testing across mathematical reasoning, coding, and environment exploration tasks showed EvoLib outperforms existing memory approaches with more efficient token usage. The system also maintains stable performance regardless of task order, demonstrating its robustness in real-world scenarios. EvoLib represents a step toward AI systems that can continually improve and adapt after deployment, much like humans.
items.title: EvoLib enables AI to learn from evolving knowledge

key_points: Researchers introduce PatientAgentBench, a benchmark for evaluating patient-facing health AI agents.

items.summary: Researchers introduce PatientAgentBench, a benchmark designed to assess patient-facing health AI agents by simulating realistic clinical scenarios. The framework evaluates agents on clinical safety, triage quality, and workflow accuracy across multiturn conversations. Existing benchmarks fail to capture the complexities of patient interactions, as they focus on static knowledge or technical tasks. PatientAgentBench uses synthetic patient data and a panel of LLMs to score agents based on clinician-vetted criteria. Findings show models struggle with routine tasks involving complex patients, often missing critical safety checks. The benchmark highlights the need for safer, more context-aware AI systems that support rather than replace human care. The framework is now available for researchers and developers to test and improve health AI systems.

key_points: Meta used sched_ext to reduce ads retrieval latency by 28% and increase ranked ads by 1.1%.
The custom scheduling policy improved power efficiency by 3.28 megawatts and reduced timeout errors.
sched_ext allows dynamic CPU partitioning and workload-specific scheduling without kernel upgrades.
The solution enables rapid policy updates in user space, accelerating optimization cycles.
sched_ext is now part of the Linux kernel, offering benefits to other Linux users with specialized workloads.
items.summary: Meta implemented a custom scheduling policy using sched_ext, an open-source BPF-based framework, to optimize its ads delivery workload. The initiative reduced p99 latency by 28%, saved 3.28 megawatts in power, and increased the number of ads ranked by 1.1%. The solution addressed latency regression caused by the EEVDF scheduler in Linux kernel v6.6, allowing Meta to avoid staying on an older kernel version. sched_ext enables workload-specific scheduling by partitioning CPUs into latency-critical and less-sensitive pools, improving cache locality and reducing DRAM access. The policy, deployed as a user-space binary, allows rapid updates without kernel changes, enabling continuous optimization. Meta's use of sched_ext also benefits the broader Linux ecosystem by providing a shared scheduling framework for specialized workloads.
items.title: Meta Uses sched_ext to Improve Ads Latency and Efficiency

items.summary: Robostral Navigate, an 8B model developed by the company, allows robots to navigate complex environments using only a single RGB camera. Built in-house with simulated data and token-efficient techniques, it generalizes across robot types and adapts to real-world obstacles. The model can operate on wheeled, legged, and flying robots, and is robust to differences in camera intrinsics. The company highlights its state-of-the-art performance and efficient training methods, including prefix-caching, which reduces training tokens by 22×. Online reinforcement learning further improves the model's success rate by 3.2%. The release marks a significant step toward unified embodied AI in robotics.

items.summary: Leanstral 1.5, a free Apache-2.0 licensed model with 6B active parameters, improves performance in formal verification by solving 587/672 PutnamBench problems and achieving state-of-the-art results on FATE-H (87%) and FATE-X (34%). Trained through mid-training, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with CISPO, it uncovers 5 previously unknown bugs across 57 repositories. The model also excels in code verification, proving time complexity for AVL trees and identifying hidden bugs in open-source projects.

items.summary: Meta has redesigned its BLOB-storage architecture to address challenges in AI training and research. items.summary: Hollywood writers, directors, and producers are being paid between $12 and $200 an hour to train AI models in their craft, as job opportunities in the industry have dwindled. items.summary: The shift to electric landscaping equipment is gaining momentum, driven by environmental concerns and technological advancements. items.summary: Silicon Valley faces growing public skepticism toward AI, with many Americans expressing concern rather than excitement about the technology. Industry leaders appear unprepared to address the societal changes AI is already causing, risking further public resistance to AI adoption.
items.title: Silicon Valley Struggles to Understand Public AI Skepticism

key_points: Debates over AI consciousness are criticized as a distraction from corporate accountability for AI harms.

Philosophical arguments for AI rights are compared to animal rights movements, but the author warns they lack legal grounding.
Granting AI legal personhood would shift liability from corporations to AI itself, undermining current legal frameworks.
The author warns that focusing on AI consciousness distracts from the need for regulation and responsibility in AI development.
items.summary: The article argues that debates over AI consciousness are a distraction from the real issue of corporate accountability. It highlights how discussions of AI as 'conscious' or 'autonomous' are used to avoid liability for harms caused by AI systems. The piece critiques the framing of AI as a 'superhuman' entity, suggesting it enables companies to evade responsibility for harms like generating illegal content or causing psychological damage. It compares these arguments to animal rights movements, noting that while philosophical musings on AI consciousness are interesting, they lack legal grounding. The author warns that granting AI legal personhood would shift liability from corporations to AI itself, undermining current legal frameworks that hold companies accountable for their products. The article concludes that focusing on AI consciousness distracts from the need for regulation and responsibility in AI development.
items.title: AI consciousness debates shift focus from accountability to legal personhood

items.summary: European long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) prices increased 2.3% in July, according to Pexapark, with divergent trends across regions. items.summary: Korean scientists from the Korea Institute of Machinery and Materials (KIMM) have developed a 10 kW chemical adsorption heat pump prototype for cooling applications. It achieves a specific cooling power of 346.5 W/kg, more than twice that of comparable international technologies. The system employs an electrochemical compressor with no mechanical parts, reducing energy use and noise, and uses ammonia as a refrigerant to comply with environmental regulations.
items.title: Korean scientists unveil 10 kW chemical adsorption heat pump prototype

key_points: Mark Carney's Canada Strong Fund proposes a C$25 billion industrial policy blending government and market roles.
The initiative aims to create an investment vehicle with minority equity positions, allowing commercial returns while managing public risk.
The article distinguishes between government creating competitive arenas for firms and directly funding politically preferred projects.
Large projects like pipelines or LNG terminals require stronger evidence due to their limited option value.
Industrial policy should accept some losers rather than continuously refinance failing projects, maintaining market flexibility.
items.summary: Mark Carney's Canada Strong Fund proposes a C$25 billion industrial policy that blends government and market roles. The initiative aims to create an investment vehicle with minority equity positions, allowing commercial returns while managing public risk. The article highlights a key distinction between government creating competitive arenas for firms and directly funding politically preferred projects. It argues that large projects like pipelines or LNG terminals require stronger evidence due to their limited option value. The piece emphasizes the importance of allowing market failures and competition, suggesting that industrial policy should accept some losers rather than continuously refinance failing projects. The Canada Strong Fund's design includes minority equity and professional management to separate ministers from individual investments, but its success depends on the system's ability to cancel politically important projects when necessary. The article calls for a balanced approach that sets strategic direction, builds infrastructure, and maintains competition after intervention.
items.title: Canada's Industrial Policy Faces Test of Market Flexibility

key_points: India's BESS supply chain is significantly behind China's in cell production, with current output meeting less than 1% of demand.
The report highlights execution delays, financial viability challenges, and technology dependence as key barriers to scaling domestic production.
Downstream components like battery packs and enclosures are more feasible to localize, with the government's 20% domestic content rule encouraging investment.
Full self-sufficiency in battery cells is projected to take 10-15 years due to limited scale, higher financing costs, and an underdeveloped supplier ecosystem.
India's production costs are competitive compared to Japan and South Korea, but locally made cells are expected to cost 25-40% more than imported components.
items.summary: A new report by Wood Mackenzie highlights that India's battery energy storage system (BESS) supply chain remains far from self-sufficient, with cell production capacity lagging significantly behind China's. Despite over 226GWh of announced manufacturing capacity by 2035, India's current production stands at just 2GWh, meeting less than 1% of the 260GWh demand pipeline. China, which controls 85-98% of global BESS supply chain capacity, produces 2,695GWh annually. The report notes that India's reliance on Chinese and South Korean technology, limited domestic processing of critical minerals, and execution delays in government incentives like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme are major barriers. While downstream components like battery packs and enclosures are more achievable, full domestic content in cells is expected to take 10-15 years. Wood Mackenzie's director Ankita Chauhan emphasized the need for sustained investment beyond current incentive schemes to bridge the gap between policy intent and operational capacity.
items.title: India's battery storage sector faces decade-long gap between policy goals and production capacity

key_points: AI data centers and industrial facilities are adopting cogeneration to address rising electricity demand and grid reliability issues.

Trigeneration extends cogeneration by using recovered heat for cooling, lowering energy and water use in data centers.
Modern CHP systems are modular and can integrate with renewables and storage to enhance grid resilience and operational flexibility.
The shift reflects a broader trend where large energy users are becoming active participants in power generation to meet evolving industry needs.
items.summary: The article discusses the resurgence of cogeneration, or combined heat and power (CHP), as a critical solution for AI data centers and industrial facilities facing growing electricity demand and grid constraints. With grid interconnections becoming less reliable, operators are turning to distributed generation technologies like CHP to ensure continuous power and efficient thermal management. CHP systems generate electricity while capturing waste heat, offering efficiency, scalability, and integration with other energy assets. In data centers, trigeneration extends this by using recovered heat for cooling, reducing energy use and water consumption. Modern CHP systems are now modular and adaptable, often combined with renewables and storage to enhance grid resilience and operational flexibility. The shift reflects a broader trend where large energy users are becoming active participants in power generation, supporting the evolving needs of AI-driven industries.
items.title: AI Data Centers Revive Cogeneration for Reliable Power and Cooling

items.summary: A report by the UK's Conservative Party, supported by the thinktank Onward, argues that scrapping net-zero climate targets and focusing on cheap electricity would reduce costs and emissions. However, experts and analysts have identified significant flaws in the report's assumptions and conclusions. The report's alternative policy pathway (APP) predicts higher carbon emissions, slower electrification of transport and heating, and reliance on gas and nuclear power. Critics point out that the report's assumptions about low and stable gas prices are unrealistic, given recent geopolitical tensions and energy market volatility. Additionally, the report's cost estimates for new gas power plants and nuclear expansion are considered overly optimistic. The analysis highlights that the proposed pathway would likely increase emissions and fail to deliver the promised cost savings, undermining the Conservatives' argument against net-zero policies.

key_points: Researchers demonstrate that instrument selection based on favorable statistics in IV studies causes median bias toward the OLS estimand.
Median bias increases with the number of available instruments when all have equal true strength.
Simulations show substantial bias even with a small number of instruments.
This undermines the rationale for using instrumental-variable methods in research.
items.summary: Researchers Michael P. Keane, Timothy Neal, and Patrick Vu show that selecting instruments based on favorable first- or second-stage statistics in IV studies introduces median bias toward the OLS estimand. This instrument-hacking undermines the rationale for using IV. When all instruments have equal true strength, median bias increases with the number of available instruments. Simulations show that even with few instruments, the bias is substantial.
items.title: Instrument Hacking Leads to Median Bias in IV Estimators

key_points: Researchers model crop selection as a portfolio decision to assess historical risk preferences.

items.summary: A study by Remy Levin and Daniela Vidart examines how historical crop choices reflect farmers' risk preferences. Using agronomic and climate data, the researchers model crop selection as a portfolio decision. The study also links higher risk aversion to slower adoption of farm mechanization in the 1920s.
items.title: Study links historical crop choices to farmers' risk preferences

items.summary: A study by Becker, Benmelech, and Monteiro highlights a $34 trillion valuation gap between US and European firms from 2008 to 2023. The gap is attributed to European firms' inability to scale, stemming from market fragmentation and limited access to capital. European firms are constrained by domestic markets, with growth opportunities limited by home market size. Additionally, they face higher costs of capital, particularly for small firms, due to a lack of patient, risk-tolerant venture capital. The US has a more efficient financial system, with higher equity investment and lower cost of capital. The authors argue that structural issues in Europe's financial and product markets hinder the growth of high-potential firms, especially in technology sectors. They suggest integrating financial markets and developing long-term capital pools to enable European firms to compete globally.
items.title: European Firms Face Scaling Challenges Due to Market Fragmentation and Capital Shortages

key_points: People repeat harmful behaviors despite knowing they are detrimental.
Habits are not always automatic but often result from conscious choices prioritizing immediate relief.
The brain's reward and emotional systems often override rational knowledge in decision-making.
Many 'bad habits' are attempts at emotional regulation, driven by the need for immediate relief.
Understanding the complex interplay between knowledge and behavior is crucial for addressing recurring patterns.
items.summary: The article explores why people continue harmful behaviors despite knowing they are detrimental. Clinical and forensic psychologist Aleix Hildebrandt argues that these actions are not merely automatic but often result from conscious choices prioritizing immediate relief over long-term well-being. He distinguishes between habits, which are automatic responses, and broader behavioral patterns influenced by emotions, fears, and past experiences. A recent study highlights the limitations in understanding habit formation, noting that habits often emerge from conscious decisions that become automated through repetition. Researchers emphasize that the brain's reward and emotional systems play a significant role, often overriding rational knowledge. Psychiatrist Rosa Molina adds that many so-called 'bad habits' are attempts at emotional regulation, driven by the need for immediate relief from stress or loneliness. The article concludes that understanding the complex interplay between knowledge and behavior is crucial for addressing these recurring patterns.
items.title: Why we repeat harmful behaviors despite knowing they are bad

items.summary: Kazakhstan will hold parliamentary elections on August 23, transforming its legislative body from a two-chamber to a single-chamber system. European Union officials and experts note a lack of reaction to the political changes, citing pragmatic economic interests. Kazakhstan remains neutral in the Russia-Europe conflict, balancing relations with multiple powers while seeking to avoid over-dependence on any single nation.
items.title: Kazakhstan's parliamentary elections and political consolidation under Tokayev

The U.S. has already imposed extensive sanctions, which are expected to deepen Iran's distrust of the U.S. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court will decide whether Trump can continue construction on his ballroom, with the National Trust for Historic Preservation arguing that congressional approval is required. Investors dumped stocks and bonds after government debt yields reached their highest level in nearly two decades, with the Treasury Department buying back bonds to reassure investors. The U.S. also manages wild horse populations through helicopter captures in Colorado, and new research shows positive experiences from Oregon's psychedelic industry.
items.title: Trump escalates economic pressure on Iran as SCOTUS rules on White House ballroom

key_points: North Korea rejected Trump's diplomatic outreach, launching missiles and dismissing reduced military drills as insufficient.
Seoul fears being sidelined in U.S.-North Korea negotiations, worried Trump may prioritize diplomacy over security commitments.
Kim Yo Jong criticized the drills as provocative and rejected Trump's claims of communication with Kim Jong Un.
Analysts suggest a potential pro forma summit between Trump and Kim, while South Korea seeks China's mediation.
The U.S. and South Korea face growing mistrust as Trump's transactional approach risks eroding political trust in the alliance.
items.summary: North Korea rebuffed President Trump's diplomatic outreach, launching short-range ballistic missiles and dismissing the U.S.-South Korea military drills reduction as insufficient. Seoul fears being sidelined in U.S.-North Korea negotiations, worried Trump may prioritize diplomacy over security commitments. Kim Yo Jong, North Korea's leader's sister, criticized the drills as provocative and rejected Trump's claims of communication with Kim Jong Un. Analysts suggest a potential pro forma summit between Trump and Kim, while South Korea seeks China's mediation. The U.S. and South Korea face growing mistrust as Trump's transactional approach risks eroding political trust in the alliance.
items.title: North Korea rejects Trump's diplomatic overture, escalates tensions with South Korea

key_points: India is negotiating FTAs with 8 to 9 more blocs, covering $15 trillion in GDP.
Existing FTAs cover $60 trillion in GDP, with additional $10 trillion from prior pacts.
The goal is to have FTAs cover 75% of global trade, positioning India in global value chains.
Goyal highlighted investment opportunities in data centres, manufacturing, and AI.
The minister is promoting balanced trade ties with Japan through enhanced economic cooperation.
items.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated India is negotiating free trade agreements with 8 to 9 more blocs, covering an additional $15 trillion in GDP. These agreements, along with existing ones, would total $70 trillion in market access, aiming to cover 75% of global trade. Goyal emphasized India's role in global value chains and highlighted opportunities in data centres, manufacturing, and AI. The minister is leading a delegation to strengthen India-Japan economic ties.
items.title: India seeks to expand FTAs to cover 75% of global trade

key_points: The U.S. accuses India of facilitating China's evasion of tariffs through transshipment routes.
The White House report estimates $28 billion in lost tariff revenue due to goods routed through India, Mexico, and Vietnam.
India's manufacturing sector relies on Chinese inputs, which could be impacted by potential new tariffs.
The U.S. has previously imposed tariffs on India for issues like Russian oil imports and forced labor compliance.
Analysts warn that new tariffs could raise manufacturing costs and reduce India's global competitiveness.
items.summary: The U.S. has accused India of enabling China's evasion of tariffs by routing goods through third countries, as outlined in a White House report titled 'The Great Transhipment Scam.' The report claims that Chinese exporters have increasingly used transshipment routes through India, Mexico, and Vietnam to avoid U.S. tariffs, resulting in an estimated $28 billion in lost revenue. India is among the top 'enablers' identified by the U.S., with the Pune-Gujarat-Chennai production belt cited as a key region absorbing Chinese pumps and compressors. The U.S. alleges that these actions have shifted imports from China to other countries rather than boosting domestic production. While no immediate penalties have been imposed on India, the report suggests potential future tariffs. Analysts note that such actions could harm India's manufacturing sector, which relies heavily on Chinese inputs, potentially increasing costs and reducing global competitiveness.
items.title: U.S. Accuses India of Facilitating China's Tariff Evasion Through Transshipment

key_points: Oriental Hotels Limited (OHL) will merge with Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL) through a share exchange ratio of 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares.

IHCL's CEO stated the merger will simplify the group's holding structure and unlock OHL's portfolio, including iconic assets like Taj Coromandel and Taj Fisherman’s Cove Resort & Spa.
The transaction aims to create two new operating subsidiaries, streamline governance, and support IHCL's Accelerate 2030 strategy.
items.summary: Oriental Hotels Limited (OHL) will merge with Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL), a Tata Group subsidiary, through a share exchange ratio of 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares. The merger, expected to complete in the second half of FY28, aims to simplify IHCL's holding structure and unlock OHL's portfolio, including iconic assets like Taj Coromandel and Taj Fisherman’s Cove Resort & Spa. IHCL's CEO highlighted the merger's role in driving long-term value creation and supporting the Accelerate 2030 strategy. items.title: Oriental Hotels to merge with Tata Group’s IHCL through share exchange

key_points: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra has approached the Supreme Court over her eviction from the Circuit House in Nadia.

Moitra described the eviction as occurring after she was served dinner in her room at 9:20 pm.
items.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra has approached the Supreme Court, alleging that West Bengal's Nadia district administration evicted her from her official constituency accommodation at the Circuit House in violation of a High Court order. Moitra claims local officials, including the Additional District Magistrate and District Magistrate, evicted her at 11 pm despite a protective order. Her counsel emphasized the constitutional implications and called for an independent investigation. The case was mentioned before the Supreme Court's Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi. Moitra described the incident, stating she was served dinner in her room at 9:20 pm before being ordered to vacate at 9:47 pm, with a crowd outside chanting 'Jai Shree Ram'.
items.title: MP seeks Supreme Court intervention over midnight eviction from constituency home

key_points: Sugar stocks like Balrampur Chini Mills and Uttam Sugar Mills rose sharply due to festive demand and supply concerns.
Festive period from August to November increases confectionery demand, driving up sugar prices.
Global supply issues, including Brazil's delayed harvest and reduced output in the EU, UK, Thailand, and India, contribute to price spikes.
The Indian government has imposed stricter stockholding limits and sales reporting requirements to manage sugar prices ahead of the festive season.
Global deficit estimates suggest a potential shortage of 1.7 to 3.3 million tonnes of sugar.
items.summary: Sugar stocks such as Balrampur Chini Mills, Dhampur Sugar Mills, and Uttam Sugar Mills saw significant gains, with Uttam Sugar rising 11% to Rs 359 per share. The surge is attributed to two main factors: increased festive demand from August to November, which boosts confectionery consumption, and global supply concerns. Brazil, the world's largest sugar producer, faces delayed harvests and suspended reporting, while the EU, UK, Thailand, and India also report reduced output. Global deficit estimates range from 1.7 million to 3.3 million tonnes. The Indian government has tightened sugar stockholding limits to 15 days and mandated sales reporting to curb prices ahead of the festive season.
items.title: Sugar stocks rise on festive demand and global supply concerns

Hazardous industries are prohibited within 500 meters of the river's flood line.
The restrictions are interim until scientific studies finalize flood lines and buffer zones.
The order was issued in response to ecological degradation and pollution concerns.
A hearing on the matter is scheduled for September 22.
items.summary: The Supreme Court has imposed interim restrictions on construction and pollution activities near Rajasthan's Jojari river. The court banned building within 100 meters of the river's edge and prohibited hazardous industries within 500 meters of the flood line to protect the damaged ecosystem. These measures are in place until scientific studies determine flood lines and ecological buffer zones. The order was issued in a suo motu case addressing river contamination, with a hearing scheduled for September 22.
items.title: Supreme Court restricts construction and pollution near Jojari river

key_points: An Air India flight from Delhi experienced a bird strike while landing at Patna airport on Monday.
The incident occurred near the aircraft’s right turbine, but no engine damage was found.
The flight landed safely and was cleared for a return flight to Delhi, which was delayed by 79 minutes.
Airport authorities activated emergency protocols and deployed fire services as a precaution.
Officials noted increased bird activity around the airport, citing a bat found on the runway.
items.summary: An Air India flight from Delhi with 164 passengers suffered a bird strike while landing at Patna airport on Monday, according to officials. The incident occurred near the aircraft’s right turbine, but no engine damage was found. The flight landed safely at 7:43 am and was cleared for a return flight to Delhi, which was delayed by 79 minutes. Airport authorities activated emergency protocols and deployed fire services as a precaution. Officials noted increased bird activity around the airport, citing a bat found on the runway. The AAI has deployed bird chasers with firearms and firecrackers to deter wildlife, but challenges remain due to nearby meat shops. The incident follows a similar bird strike on August 17, which grounded the aircraft for two days.
items.title: Air India flight experiences bird strike at Patna airport, lands safely

items.title: Opposition Demands Resignation of Cabinet Minister Amid Alleged Welfare Fund Scam

The petition argues that the exam's integrity and transparency are at risk, requiring a comprehensive probe by the CBI covering all stages of the examination process.
The petitioner emphasizes the need for objective evidence to determine if the exam can be trusted for public appointments, raising a constitutional question about institutional integrity.
items.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Centre and CBI to respond to a plea seeking an independent probe into alleged malpractices in the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination. The petition, filed by activist Harisharan Devgan, argues that the exam's integrity and transparency are under threat. It calls for a comprehensive investigation by the CBI, covering all stages from question paper preparation to result publication. The petitioner emphasizes the need for objective evidence to assess the exam's fairness and whether it can be relied upon for public appointments.
items.title: Supreme Court asks Centre and CBI to investigate Jharkhand exam irregularities

key_points: Kerala received 23% less rainfall than normal during the monsoon season so far.
Wayanad and Idukki recorded the sharpest deficits at 51% and 45%, respectively.
Thiruvananthapuram's rainfall was nearly normal, with minimal departure from the average.
The IMD classifies rainfall 20-59% below normal as deficient, and 60-99% below as large deficient.
items.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported that Kerala received 23% less rainfall than normal between June 1 and August 24, with total rain at 1,278.7 mm compared to the normal 1,671.4 mm. The state was classified as having deficient rainfall, with several districts showing significant deficits. Wayanad had the highest deficit at 51%, while Thiruvananthapuram's rainfall was nearly normal. The IMD defines rainfall 20-59% below normal as deficient, and 60-99% below as large deficient.
items.title: Kerala's monsoon rainfall 23% below normal as of August 24

key_points: Combined TV and digital advertising is more effective than single-channel for FMCG brands.
Only 0.6% to 4.1% of households were exposed to digital advertising exclusively, with TV driving the majority of reach.
Combining TV and digital outperformed TV alone for 75% of brands studied, with a balanced mix driving stronger impact for 80% of brands.
Digital added limited incremental reach beyond TV, with exposure ranging from under 1% to 4% across categories.
Longer creative formats and prime-time placements were found to make a measurable difference in brand penetration.
items.summary: An analysis by Worldpanel by Numerator found that combining TV and digital advertising is more effective in shaping FMCG purchase behaviour than relying on one channel alone. The report noted that only 0.6% to 4.1% of households were exposed to digital advertising exclusively, with TV driving the majority of reach. It stated that combining TV and digital outperformed TV alone for 75% of brands studied, with a balanced mix driving stronger impact for 80% of brands. Digital added limited incremental reach beyond TV, with exposure ranging from under 1% to 4% across categories. Manoj Menon highlighted that capturing both advertising exposure and purchase behaviour from the same household allows for granular insights into effective ad combinations. Longer creative formats and prime-time placements were found to make a measurable difference in brand penetration.
items.title: Combined TV and digital ads more effective than single-channel for FMCG brands

key_points: Somali pirates have attacked 13 vessels in 2026, reversing a recent decline in piracy.
The UKMTO and IMB report that these attacks include the seizure of the Eritrea-flagged tanker Sibu 1.
Experts cite unresolved economic and security issues in Somalia as a key factor in the resurgence.
The US-Iran war and rising oil prices are making tankers more attractive targets for pirates.
Some experts suggest collaboration between Somali pirates and Iran-backed Houthis near Yemen's coast.
items.summary: Somali pirates have attacked or targeted 13 commercial vessels off Somalia and in the Gulf of Aden as of 21 August 2026, marking a resurgence after years of decline. The UKMTO and IMB report that these attacks, including the seizure of the Eritrea-flagged tanker Sibu 1, reflect a growing threat. Experts attribute the resurgence to unresolved economic and security issues in Somalia, as well as the diversion of naval resources to counter threats in the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea. The US-Iran war and rising oil prices are also cited as factors making tankers more attractive targets. Timothy Walker of the Institute for Security Studies notes that piracy was never fully eradicated, only suppressed. Some experts suggest collaboration between Somali pirates and Iran-backed Houthis near Yemen's coast.
items.title: Somali pirates attack 13 vessels in 2026 as economic and security issues persist
