The system uses 5 MWh lithium iron phosphate battery blocks and liquid cooling to meet utility requirements for rapid load management.
Cummins positions battery storage as part of a broader power architecture for AI facilities, not a standalone replacement for conventional generation.
The project represents a shift for Cummins beyond traditional power generation, emphasizing battery storage for modern data centre resilience.
items.summary: Cummins has secured its largest battery energy storage system (BESS) order to date for a US data centre, aimed at managing electricity demand fluctuations from AI workloads. The system uses 5 MWh lithium iron phosphate battery blocks and liquid cooling, designed to meet utility requirements for rapid load management and grid stability. Cummins emphasized that the BESS supports data centres alongside diesel and natural gas power systems, positioning it as part of a broader power architecture for AI facilities. The project marks a shift for Cummins beyond traditional power generation, highlighting battery storage as a critical component for modern data centre resilience.
items.title: Cummins supplies largest BESS for US data centre to manage AI workload demand

key_points: The Port of Corpus Christi has partnered with MARAD to explore nuclear maritime technologies.
The initiative includes assessing small modular reactors, microgrids, and infrastructure for future vessel propulsion.
A separate study with Core Power will evaluate floating nuclear power plants and nuclear-powered commercial ships.
The study is a preliminary fact-finding exercise without committing to licensing or construction.
The Port aims to maintain its competitive edge in the global energy marketplace through these efforts.
items.summary: The Port of Corpus Christi has signed a memorandum of cooperation with the US Maritime Administration (MARAD) to explore nuclear maritime technologies, making it the second US port to formalise such a partnership. The initiative aims to advance maritime energy systems through small modular reactors (SMRs), resilient port microgrids, and infrastructure for emerging vessel propulsion concepts. The collaboration also includes a study with UK-based Core Power to assess floating nuclear power plants (FNPPs) and readiness for nuclear-powered commercial ships. The partners will examine technical, environmental, and regulatory requirements for FNPP deployment and safe operations of nuclear vessels. Core Power emphasized the study is a preliminary fact-finding exercise without committing to licensing or construction. The Port of Corpus Christi, as a major energy gateway, seeks to maintain its competitive edge in the evolving global energy marketplace through these efforts.
items.title: Port of Corpus Christi and MARAD partner on nuclear maritime tech exploration

key_points: PJM proposes a new framework to manage data center load growth without requiring full upfront capacity.
The IRAS system would allow uncovered load to be used as a reliability resource during emergencies.
A Large Load Registry and Bring Your Own New Capacity (BYONC) mechanism are key components of the plan.
Data center demand is projected to increase by 32 GW by 2030, contributing to capacity shortages.
PJM plans a Reliability Backstop Procurement to address remaining capacity gaps, with costs allocated to load-serving entities and states.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: PJM Interconnection has proposed a new framework to manage growing data center demand, allowing large loads to enter service without securing full capacity upfront. The plan, called IRAS, would make uncovered load available for reduction during emergencies before using existing demand-response resources. The framework includes a Large Load Registry, a Bring Your Own New Capacity (BYONC) mechanism, and compensation for load reductions. PJM aims to implement the changes by 2027, as data center growth is projected to add 32 GW of demand by 2030. The proposal follows recent capacity shortages and aims to ensure reliability amid rising load and retiring generation. PJM also plans a Reliability Backstop Procurement to cover remaining capacity gaps, with costs allocated to load-serving entities and states.
items.title: PJM Introduces New Framework to Address Data Center Load Growth

key_points: The study investigates whether occupational licensing improves service quality and safety for Uber drivers using trip-level data.
Researchers compare trips by licensed and unlicensed drivers in New York City, New Jersey, and post-deregulation Houston.
Findings show no consistent evidence that licensing leads to better consumer outcomes.
In Houston, new entrants after deregulation perform similarly to previously licensed drivers in ratings and driving behavior.
items.summary: A study by Jonathan Hall, Jason Hicks, Morris M. Kleiner, and Yun taek Oh examines whether occupational licensing enhances service quality and safety for Uber drivers. Using trip-level data, the researchers compare trips by licensed and unlicensed drivers in New York City, New Jersey, and post-deregulation Houston. They find no consistent evidence that licensing improves consumer outcomes. In Houston, new entrants after deregulation perform similarly to previously licensed drivers in ratings and driving behavior, despite differences in experience and age. The study uses quasi-random assignment and instrumental variable estimates to analyze the impact of licensing.
items.title: Uber Driver Licensing Study Finds No Consistent Improvement in Service Quality or Safety

key_points: Olivier Wang decomposes stock returns into a Treasury component linked to monetary policy surprises and a payoff component.
Stock volatility is reduced by rate insurance, where rates fall in bad times, offsetting payoff risk.
Expected stock returns are dampened as rates rise in good times, hedging losses for investors holding net duration, particularly when Ricardian equivalence fails.
The framework explains bond premia, negative stock-bond covariance, equity anomalies, and the collapse of the value premium, suggesting fiscal and monetary policy influence bond and equity premia.
It also proposes a two-factor model for pricing stocks and bonds together, and explains why long bonds outperform long stocks.
items.summary: Olivier Wang decomposes stock returns into a Treasury component linked to monetary policy surprises and a payoff component. Risk and returns for stocks increase less with duration compared to matched Treasuries. Stock volatility is reduced by rate insurance, where rates fall in bad times, offsetting payoff risk. Expected stock returns are dampened as rates rise in good times, hedging losses for investors holding net duration, particularly when Ricardian equivalence fails. The framework explains bond premia, negative stock-bond covariance, equity anomalies, and the collapse of the value premium, suggesting fiscal and monetary policy influence bond and equity premia. It also proposes a two-factor model for pricing stocks and bonds together, and explains why long bonds outperform long stocks.
items.title: Stock Returns Decomposed with Rate Insurance Framework

Ross plans to open 115 new stores in 2026, with CEO Jim Conroy emphasizing customer traffic and store expansion as key growth drivers.
items.summary: Ross Stores increased its 2026 earnings per share forecast to $8.61-$8.77, citing a 13% sales rise to $6.3bn and 47 new store openings. The company reported net income of $851m and operating profits of $1.1bn, with tariff refunds contributing to a 610 basis point margin increase. CEO Jim Conroy highlighted customer traffic and store expansion as key drivers, raising the 2026 new store target to 115 locations. For Q3 and Q4, Ross expects comparable sales growth of 6-7% and 4-5%, respectively, with EPS projections of $1.75-$1.83 and $2.17-$2.26.
items.title: Ross Stores boosts 2026 earnings forecast due to Q2 sales growth and store expansion

Next year's Eurovision will be held in Burgas, Bulgaria, following Dara's victory.
This year's event recorded 131 million viewers, a 35 million drop from last year.
items.summary: The Netherlands' public broadcaster, AVROTROS, will skip next year's Eurovision Song Contest, citing the event's 'no longer neutral' status due to conflicts over the Gaza war. Director-General Taco Zimmerman stated that international conflicts are undermining the contest's neutrality. The decision follows recent boycotts by several countries over Israel's participation, with five nations pulling out this year. Next year's contest will be held in Burgas, Bulgaria, following Dara's victory. This year's event saw a 35 million viewer drop compared to last year.
items.title: Netherlands broadcaster withdraws from Eurovision over perceived loss of neutrality

key_points: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Iran of an 'economic D-Day' to cut all financial ties and isolate its partners.
Iran dismissed the threat, vowing to shut down oil exports if the conflict continues.
The Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil route, has been effectively blocked by Iran since February.
Bessent's comments followed previous US threats, including Trump's April warning of a 'civilisation dying' unless Iran unblocked the strait.
The US has imposed tough sanctions on Iran since 2018, after pulling out of the 2015 nuclear deal.
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Iran of an 'economic D-Day' to sever all financial ties, threatening to isolate any nation partnering with the country. Iran dismissed the comments, vowing to shut down oil exports if the conflict continues. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil route, has been effectively blocked by Iran since February. Bessent's remarks followed previous US threats, including Trump's April warning of a 'civilisation dying' unless Iran unblocked the strait. The US has imposed tough sanctions on Iran since 2018, after pulling out of the 2015 nuclear deal. Biden's attempts to reinstate the deal failed, and recent sanctions targeted foreign firms doing business with Tehran.
items.title: US Treasury Secretary warns of economic D-Day against Iran

key_points: Creditors of Thames Water propose a board overhaul to avoid nationalisation.
The plan includes appointing experienced executives like Liz Barber and Clive Selley.
Critics accuse the proposal of being a superficial change that ignores public interests.
The consortium seeks to reassure the government about leadership changes in a potential commercial deal.
The proposal faces scrutiny amid concerns over rising water bills and government intervention.
items.summary: Creditors of Thames Water, led by London & Valley Water, have proposed a board overhaul to avoid nationalisation. The plan includes appointing Liz Barber, Clive Selley, and Dame Bernadette Kelly as directors, with Mike McTighe becoming chair. The consortium aims to reassure the government that a commercial deal would bring leadership changes. Critics, including We Own It, accuse the plan of being a 'deckchair shuffle' that ignores public interests. The proposal comes amid concerns over rising water bills and potential government intervention through a special administration regime.
items.title: Creditors propose board overhaul for Thames Water to avoid nationalisation

items.summary: The Trump administration is escalating economic pressure on Iran with 'toughest sanctions in history,' aiming to isolate Tehran through a naval blockade and financial restrictions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that any country engaging in trade with Iran will face severe consequences. Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the measures as an 'erosion of sovereignty,' while Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned of 'seismic' retaliation against nations joining the sanctions. Analysts note that China and Russia, key trading partners of Iran, may resist U.S. pressure due to their limited reliance on the American financial system. Gulf states remain divided on whether to support U.S. sanctions, fearing regional instability if Iran collapses.
items.title: US threatens economic sanctions against Iran, Iran vows retaliation

key_points: Canadian and US businesses are bracing for the fallout of escalating trade tensions and new tariffs.
Business owners like Cindy Baldassi warn that half their business could be lost due to increased costs.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced tariffs on US goods starting September 8, while US tariffs on Canadian products took effect immediately.
Small businesses are particularly vulnerable, with owners like Matteo Sgaramella struggling to manage rising costs and potential losses.
The trade war is affecting various sectors, including retail, wine, and craft businesses, with some companies facing reduced market access and higher costs.
items.summary: Canadian and US businesses are facing significant challenges due to escalating trade tensions between the two nations. The imposition of 50% tariffs on each other's products has raised concerns among business owners, with many fearing a decline in sales and potential closures. Cindy Baldassi, a Calgary-based jeweler, warns that half her business could be lost due to increased costs. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced tariffs on US goods starting September 8, while US tariffs on Canadian products took effect immediately. Business owners like Michael Saifer of Lind Furniture and Matteo Sgaramella of Outclass are struggling to navigate the new economic landscape, with small businesses particularly vulnerable. The impact extends beyond trade, affecting companies like Paloma Clothing and Terre Rouge Wines, which face higher costs and reduced market access. Heather Seevers of Northwest Yarns and Mercantile reports a drop in Canadian customers and increased community support efforts to sustain her business amid the trade war.
items.title: Canadian and US businesses brace for trade war fallout

key_points: Childhood exposure to joint custody reforms reduces adult fertility by 7 percent.
The effect is symmetric for both men and women and occurs through lower parenthood and couple formation.
Exposed individuals exhibit sub-additive effects within couples and assortatively match.
The study suggests family preferences form during childhood, contributing to declining US fertility rates.
items.summary: A study by Daniel Fernández-Kranz and Sébastien Fontenay finds that childhood exposure to joint custody reforms reduces adult fertility by 7 percent, affecting both men and women equally. The effect is primarily through reduced parenthood and couple formation, with sub-additive impacts within couples. Exposed individuals also tend to assortatively match. The research highlights the development of family preferences during childhood and links the US fertility decline to rising childlessness and declining couple formation.
items.title: Childhood Joint Custody Exposure Linked to Lower Adult Fertility

key_points: The UK government must decide whether to approve oil and gas drilling at Rosebank and Jackdaw fields, with differing environmental and energy implications.
A court ruled previous environmental assessments for the fields were incomplete, failing to account for emissions from burning the extracted oil and gas.
Jackdaw could contribute to energy security by displacing dirtier LNG imports, while Rosebank would generate significant emissions over 25 years, conflicting with net zero targets.
Rosebank should only be approved if it meets carbon capture and storage (CCS) conditions, a technology already used by Equinor.
The government is urged to accelerate decommissioning of aging fields and publish a net zero transition roadmap to address economic and climate concerns.
items.summary: The UK government must decide whether to approve oil and gas drilling at Rosebank and Jackdaw fields, with differing environmental and energy implications. The Conservative government previously granted licenses in 2022 and 2023, but a court ruled their environmental assessments were incomplete, failing to account for emissions from burning the extracted oil and gas. The new energy and climate secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, must assess if updated assessments justify approval. Jackdaw, a small gasfield, could contribute to energy security by displacing dirtier LNG imports, while Rosebank, a large oilfield, would generate significant emissions over 25 years, conflicting with net zero targets. The article argues that Rosebank should only be approved if it meets carbon capture and storage (CCS) conditions, a technology already used by Equinor. The government is also urged to accelerate decommissioning of aging fields and publish a net zero transition roadmap to address economic and climate concerns.
items.title: UK Government Faces Decision on Oil Drilling Conditions Amid Climate and Energy Pressures

The US sanctioned Akane and ICC prosecutor Abdoulaye Seye, who was involved in seeking an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over alleged war crimes in Gaza.
items.title: Japan reaffirms support for ICC president amid criticism of muted response to US sanctions

key_points: Zerra DC proposes a $31.9 billion data centre in Queensland's Western Downs region.
The project would require substantial water during construction and operation, prompting concerns about water security.
Federal government is finalizing new rules requiring data centres to use renewable energy.
Local councils in Southern Queensland seek to protect drinking water sources from data centre expansion.
Queensland's Minister for Water highlights the need for community consultation on the proposal.
items.summary: Singapore-based developer Zerra DC has proposed a $31.9 billion data centre in regional Queensland, raising concerns about energy and water use. The Western Downs Digital Park, near Dalby, would prioritize air-cooled technology but still require significant water during construction and operation. The federal government is finalizing new rules requiring data centres to use renewable energy, while local councils in Southern Queensland push to protect drinking water sources. Queensland's Minister for Water emphasized community consultation on the project.
items.title: Zerra DC proposes $31.9 billion data centre in Queensland amid energy and water concerns

key_points: Japanese clinics are offering 'beauty sleep' treatments involving prescription drugs.
Experts criticize the use of psychotropic medications for cosmetic purposes.
The treatments are not covered by public health insurance, increasing patient costs.
The Japanese Society of Sleep Research advises against long-term use of sleeping pills for non-medical reasons.
Clinics are advised to prioritize lifestyle changes before prescribing medication for insomnia.
items.summary: Japanese clinics are promoting 'beauty sleep' treatments that include psychotropic drugs and sleeping pills, sparking controversy. Experts criticize the practice, noting these medications are not intended for cosmetic use and may lead to dependence. The treatments, not covered by public health insurance, have raised concerns about inappropriate prescription practices. The Japanese Society of Sleep Research advises against long-term use of such medications for non-medical purposes. Kurume University's president warns that sleeping pills should be used only for insomnia treatment, not for beauty enhancement.
items.title: Japanese Clinics Offer Beauty Sleep Treatments with Prescription Drugs

key_points: Researchers identified immune hubs in mouse skull bone marrow that respond to brain tumors more effectively than distant lymph nodes.
Disrupting these hubs in mice with glioblastoma led to faster tumor growth and earlier death, while stimulating them improved tumor rejection and survival.
The study challenges the traditional view of the brain as immune-privileged and suggests the skull may play a role in defending the brain.
The findings, published in Nature, remain preliminary as the structures have only been demonstrated in mice, and their existence and function in humans are yet to be confirmed.
The discovery could have implications for treating brain diseases, including cancer, infections, and neurodegenerative disorders, if similar structures are found in humans.
items.summary: Scientists at Washington University School of Medicine discovered immune 'security stations' in the bone marrow of mouse skulls, which respond to brain tumors more effectively than distant lymph nodes. These structures, resembling lymph nodes, are located near the brain and may enable faster, localized immune responses. Disrupting these hubs in mice with glioblastoma led to faster tumor growth and earlier death, while stimulating them improved tumor rejection and survival. The findings, published in Nature, suggest the skull may have a role in defending the brain, challenging the traditional view of the brain as immune-privileged. However, the study only demonstrates these structures in mice, and their existence and function in humans remain to be confirmed. Researchers note the potential implications for treating brain diseases, including cancer, infections, and neurodegenerative disorders, if similar structures are found in humans.
items.title: Researchers identify immune hubs in skull bone marrow that respond to brain tumors

key_points: A 70-year-old Iranian woman with breast cancer cannot afford her chemotherapy due to soaring costs.
Drug prices in Iran have risen sharply, with some medications increasing by over 500%.
Experts warn that delayed treatment can lead to severe health complications and premature death.
Patients are increasingly seeking medications through unofficial channels, risking drug quality and safety.
Iran's healthcare system faces multiple pressures, including currency issues, sanctions, and war-related disruptions.
items.summary: A 70-year-old Iranian woman with advanced breast cancer faces financial barriers to her chemotherapy treatment, as one session costs six times the minimum monthly wage. Doctors in Iran report that rising drug prices, shortages, and disrupted foreign currency transfers are making healthcare increasingly unaffordable. An Iranian pharmaceutical company raised prices for 82 products by up to 543%, with insulin and cancer drugs seeing particularly steep increases. Experts warn that delayed treatment can lead to complications and premature death, especially for cancer patients. The situation reflects broader challenges in Iran's healthcare system, exacerbated by currency depreciation, sanctions, and war-related disruptions. Patients are increasingly turning to unofficial cross-border channels for medications, raising concerns about drug quality and storage conditions.
items.title: Iranian Cancer Patient Faces Financial Barriers to Chemotherapy

key_points: Ukrainian drone attacks have caused significant disruptions to Russia's energy infrastructure.
A third of Russian oil production is currently offline due to these attacks.
Russian officials are addressing the shortages through repairs and imports from neighboring countries.
The fuel crisis has reached its peak before parliamentary elections, with no clear solution to prevent future attacks.
items.summary: Russia is experiencing gas shortages caused by Ukrainian drone attacks on energy infrastructure. The attacks have disrupted oil production and logistics, with a third of Russian oil output offline. Russian officials claim to be addressing the issues through repairs and imports from countries like India and Kazakhstan. Despite government assurances, the fuel crisis has reached its peak ahead of parliamentary elections, with no clear solution to prevent future attacks.
items.title: Russia faces gas shortages due to Ukrainian strikes

key_points: The U.S. war with Iran is linked to global conflicts including Russia's war in Ukraine and tensions on the Korean Peninsula.
North Korea is providing troops to Russia, while Russia and China support Iran's military efforts.
Global disruptions, such as oil supply issues and strain on U.S. military resources, are consequences of these interconnected conflicts.
China is enhancing its military capabilities to rival the U.S., with potential implications for Taiwan.
Trump's outreach to North Korea and the strategic considerations of nuclear proliferation are discussed.
items.summary: The article discusses how the U.S. war with Iran is interconnected with other global conflicts, including Russia's war in Ukraine and tensions in the Korean Peninsula. NPR correspondents Tom Bowman and Emily Feng explain that North Korea is providing troops to Russia, while Russia and China are supporting Iran's military efforts. The article highlights the global impact of these conflicts, such as disruptions in oil supply through the Strait of Hormuz and the strain on U.S. military resources like Patriot missiles. It also notes how China is strengthening its military capabilities to rival the U.S., with potential implications for Taiwan. The discussion includes Trump's outreach to North Korea and the strategic considerations of nuclear proliferation in the region.
items.title: U.S.-Iran War Ties to Global Conflicts and Strategic Shifts

key_points: The Supreme Court has asked Jharkhand to allow a CBI investigation into exam irregularities.
A petition by activist Harisharan Devgan argues the State CID lacks impartiality.
Students have protested for over a month over alleged evaluation discrepancies.
A viral OMR carbon copy allegedly showed irregularities, triggering protests and hunger strikes.
The petition seeks to secure evidence for an unbiased probe into public officials and exam agencies.
items.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the State of Jharkhand and its Public Service Commission to respond to a petition seeking a CBI investigation into alleged malpractices in a civil services exam. The petition, filed by activist Harisharan Devgan, argues that the State Criminal Investigation Department lacks impartiality. Students have protested for over a month, citing irregularities in evaluation, including a viral OMR carbon copy showing discrepancies. The petition calls for securing physical and digital evidence, including CCTV footage and server logs, to ensure an unbiased probe.
items.title: Supreme Court asks Jharkhand to allow CBI probe into exam irregularities

key_points: Tamil Nadu's government will abandon the Parandur airport project due to land and settlement concerns.
Terminal 5 at Chennai airport's northwest area is proposed as an alternative development.
The decision followed protests and opposition demands, which were blocked by the Assembly Speaker.
The new terminal aims to increase passenger capacity to 55 million annually, easing transport pressure.
The Chief Minister criticized the previous government for prioritizing the airport over local communities.
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced the cancellation of the Parandur airport project, citing concerns over farmland and human settlements. He proposed developing Terminal 5 at Chennai airport's northwest area with the Airports Authority of India. The decision followed protests from farmers and opposition calls for debate, which were blocked by the Speaker. Vijay emphasized that the new terminal would increase passenger capacity to 55 million annually, improving transport until a new airport is built. He criticized the previous government for prioritizing the airport over local communities.
items.title: Tamil Nadu to abandon Parandur airport plan, seeks alternative sites

key_points: Tamil Nadu's chief minister scrapped the Parandur airport plan due to land and livelihood concerns.
The government will expand Chennai's existing airport but is seeking new sites for a future airport.
DMK leaders criticized the decision, warning of economic damage and loss of investment opportunities.
The announcement led to an assembly walkout by DMK MLAs over perceived policy reversal.
Feasibility studies are underway to identify alternative locations for the new airport.
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay announced the abandonment of the Parandur greenfield airport project, citing concerns over agricultural land disruption and impact on farmers' livelihoods. The decision follows protests from residents of 12 surrounding villages, whom Vijay supported. While the government will expand Chennai's Meenambakkam airport, it is now seeking alternative sites for a new airport through feasibility studies. The DMK criticized the move, arguing it could harm industrial growth and push businesses to neighboring states. The announcement triggered an assembly walkout by DMK MLAs, who accused the government of a policy reversal.
items.title: Tamil Nadu chief minister scraps Parandur airport plan due to land concerns

key_points: MK Stalin has filed a petition with the Madras High Court challenging VS Babu's victory in Kolathur.
The petition questions the validity of the TVK candidate's win in the assembly elections.
Stalin is seeking a recount of votes in the contested constituency.
items.summary: MK Stalin, the DMK president and former Tamil Nadu chief minister, has filed a petition with the Madras High Court challenging the victory of TVK candidate VS Babu in the Kolathur assembly constituency. The legal move comes in the context of recent assembly elections, with Stalin seeking a recount of votes. The court will now consider the petition, which questions the validity of Babu's win.
items.title: MK Stalin challenges Kolathur election result in High Court

key_points: Anita Nariani Schulze, an Indian-American engineer, filed a discrimination lawsuit against Apple Inc. alleging bias based on nationality, religion, and gender.
Schulze claims her male managers excluded her from meetings, criticized her work, and denied her bonuses despite positive performance reviews.
Judge Sunil R. Kulkarni rejected Apple's motion to dismiss the case but denied Schulze's request to represent a class of female employees.
Cisco Systems faces a separate lawsuit over alleged caste-based discrimination against a Dalit employee, with the company denying the claims.
items.summary: An Indian-American engineer, Anita Nariani Schulze, has filed a discrimination lawsuit against Apple Inc., alleging that her male managers from India and Pakistan treated her with bias based on her nationality, religion, and gender. The case, filed in California state court, claims her managers excluded her from meetings, criticized her work, and denied her bonuses despite positive performance reviews. Judge Sunil R. Kulkarni rejected Apple's motion to dismiss the case but denied Schulze's request to represent a class of female employees. Meanwhile, Cisco Systems faces a separate lawsuit from California's civil rights agency over alleged caste-based discrimination against a Dalit employee. Cisco denies the claims, arguing caste is not a protected category under U.S. law.
items.title: Indian Engineer Files Bias Lawsuit Against Apple

key_points: Former Union Minister P Chidambaram opposed the 'One Nation, One Election' proposal as unconstitutional and monstrous during a parliamentary panel discussion.
Chidambaram argued that the bills violate the Constitution's basic structure by curtailing legislatures' five-year terms.
TMC's Sagarika Ghosh and some Padma awardees also opposed the bills, while others supported them.
The bills, introduced in December 2024, aim to synchronize Lok Sabha and state assembly elections following a high-level panel recommendation.
The practice of simultaneous elections was common from 1951 to 1967 but has since been disrupted by premature dissolutions and term extensions.
items.summary: Former Union Minister P Chidambaram criticized the 'One Nation, One Election' proposal as 'monstrous' and 'unconstitutional' during a parliamentary panel discussion. He argued that the bills violate the Constitution's basic structure by curtailing legislatures' five-year terms. TMC's Sagarika Ghosh and some Padma awardees also opposed the bills, while others supported them. The bills, introduced in December 2024, aim to synchronize Lok Sabha and state assembly elections, following a high-level panel recommendation. The practice of simultaneous elections was common from 1951 to 1967 but has since been disrupted by premature dissolutions and term extensions.
items.title: Chidambaram opposes 'One Nation One Election' as unconstitutional

key_points: Protests in Manipur have intensified over demands for NRC implementation before the 2027 census.
Civil society groups argue the NRC is needed to address undocumented migration and demographic shifts.
Tribal councils oppose immediate NRC rollout, claiming it deepens regional divisions.
A 48-hour strike disrupted normal life in valley districts of Manipur.
Chandigarh police uncovered a terror plot involving explosives and weapons, with three suspects arrested.
items.summary: Protests in Manipur have intensified as civil society groups demand the National Register of Citizens (NRC) be implemented before the 2027 census, citing concerns over undocumented migration and demographic changes. Tribal councils oppose immediate rollout, arguing it is premature and exacerbates regional divisions. Meanwhile, a 48-hour strike disrupted daily life in valley districts. In unrelated news, Chandigarh police uncovered a terror plot involving explosives and weapons, while political figures discussed legal actions and social audits.
items.title: Manipur Protests Escalate Over NRC Implementation Before 2027 Census

key_points: The Income Tax Department urged taxpayers with business or professional income to file ITRs by August 31, 2026, for AY 2026-27.
As of August 20, over 6.5 crore ITRs had been filed, including more than 5.9 crore ITR-1 and ITR-2 forms by July 31.
ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, and ITR-7 are applicable to non-audit category taxpayers.
ITR-6 is filed by companies under the Companies Act, while ITR-7 is for trusts and charitable institutions.
items.summary: The Income Tax Department urged taxpayers with business or professional income to file their ITRs by August 31, 2026, for the AY 2026-27 fiscal year. As of August 20, over 6.5 crore ITRs had been filed, including more than 5.9 crore ITR-1 and ITR-2 forms by the July 31 deadline. The department highlighted that ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, and ITR-7 are applicable to non-audit category taxpayers, while ITR-6 is for companies and ITR-7 for trusts and charitable institutions.
items.title: Income Tax Department Urges Taxpayers to File ITRs by August 31

key_points: The rupee declined 3 paise to 95.74 against the US dollar on Monday.
Rising crude oil prices and US sanctions on Iran weighed on investor sentiment.
The dollar index rose to 98.98, while Brent crude fell to $92.86 per barrel.
Domestic markets saw declines in the Sensex and Nifty, with foreign investors offloading equities.
India's forex reserves increased by $9.905 billion to $716.907 billion.
items.summary: The Indian rupee fell 3 paise to 95.74 against the US dollar on Monday, influenced by a strong American currency and weak domestic markets. Forex traders noted that rising Brent crude prices, importer demand, and concerns over US sanctions on Iran affected investor sentiment. The dollar index rose to 98.98, while Brent crude fell to $92.86 per barrel. Domestic markets saw the Sensex and Nifty decline, with foreign investors selling equities worth ₹542.71 crore. India's forex reserves increased by $9.905 billion to $716.907 billion.
items.title: Rupee declines 3 paise to 95.74 against dollar amid market uncertainty

key_points: The Kochi Corporation plans to repatriate residents from other states to their home care facilities before renovating the Palluruthy Relief Settlement.
The existing facility, housing 138 residents, will be replaced with a modern, self-sustaining complex featuring a wellness centre and commercial space.
Antony Painuthara noted that 30-40% of residents are from outside Kerala, and efforts are underway to restore them to their families.
Sources highlighted the urgent need for renovation, while an NGO criticized the PRS for past neglect and reduced rescue efforts.
items.summary: The Kochi Corporation is planning to repatriate residents from other states at the Palluruthy Relief Settlement to their respective care facilities, ahead of a proposed overhaul. The existing 10,000 sq. ft. facility, housing 138 residents, will be replaced with a modern, self-sustaining complex featuring a wellness centre and commercial space. Antony Painuthara, chairperson of the Corporation’s welfare committee, stated that around 30-40% of residents are from outside Kerala. The plan includes restoring residents to their families where possible. Sources noted the urgent need for renovation, while an NGO criticized the PRS for past neglect and reduced rescue efforts.
items.title: Kochi Corporation proposes repatriation of residents from other States ahead of overhaul of Palluruthy Relief Settlement

key_points: The Madras High Court extended the stay on five Tamil Nadu assembly bypolls until September 8 due to pending election petitions.
The court rejected the Tamil Nadu government's request to lift the stay on bypolls for constituencies including Trichy East, where Chief Minister C Jopseph Vijay won.
DMK president MK Stalin filed an election petition challenging the victory of TVK candidate VS Babu in Kolathur, citing alleged voting machine issues.
VS Babu attributed his victory to party chief Vijay's leadership and local connections, highlighting anti-incumbency sentiments in Tamil Nadu.
Stalin's loss to Babu, despite the DMK alliance securing over 1.54 crore votes, has sparked legal and political debate.
items.summary: The Madras High Court has extended the interim stay on notifying five Tamil Nadu assembly bypolls until September 8, as election petitions challenging the results remain pending. The court rejected the Tamil Nadu government's request to lift the stay. One bypoll was triggered by Chief Minister C Jopseph Vijay's victory in the Trichy East constituency. Meanwhile, DMK president MK Stalin filed an election petition challenging the victory of TVK candidate VS Babu in Kolathur, citing alleged voting machine malfunctions and irregularities. Stalin's loss to Babu, who attributed his win to Vijay's leadership and local connections, has sparked legal and political debate.
items.title: Madras High Court Extends Stay on Tamil Nadu Assembly Bypolls

key_points: Iran's rial fell to a record low of 2.02 million to the dollar amid US sanctions and economic strain.
The US is preparing stronger sanctions, including secondary penalties against countries trading with Iran.
Iran and Oman are close to agreeing on a plan to jointly manage the Strait of Hormuz.
The UAE suspended trade with Iran, worsening its economic situation.
Iran warns that supporting US sanctions would be considered an act of war.
items.summary: Iran's rial hit a record low of 2.02 million to the dollar as the US prepares new sanctions. The currency's decline follows months of economic strain and conflict. Despite the pressure, Iran maintains control over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil route. Iran and Oman are nearing an agreement to jointly manage the strait, amid US criticism of Oman. The US plans stronger sanctions, including secondary penalties against countries trading with Iran. The UAE has suspended trade with Iran, worsening its economic situation. Iran warns against supporting the new sanctions, calling it an act of war.
items.title: US sanctions push Iranian rial to record low as tensions over Hormuz persist

key_points: Maharashtra requires taxi drivers to demonstrate working knowledge of Marathi under new 2026 rules.
The regulation raises constitutional concerns under Article 19, which protects the right to practice a profession.
Legal experts warn that tying employment to linguistic ability could undermine free movement across states.
The rule has faced similar challenges before, with courts previously rejecting similar conditions.
Critics argue the requirement may impose undue burdens on drivers whose essential functions are unrelated to language proficiency.
items.summary: Maharashtra has introduced a rule requiring taxi and autorickshaw drivers to demonstrate a working knowledge of Marathi, raising constitutional concerns. The 2026 amendment to the Motor Vehicles Rules mandates that drivers prove language proficiency, with failure leading to potential suspension or revocation of their permits. The state argues this ensures effective communication with passengers, but critics highlight that the regulation risks conflating language proficiency with occupational competence. Article 19 of the Constitution protects the right to practice a profession, and legal experts warn that tying employment to linguistic ability could undermine the principle of free movement across states. The rule has faced similar challenges before, with courts previously rejecting similar conditions. While the state has leeway to regulate transport, the proportionality of the Marathi requirement remains questionable, as it may impose undue burdens on drivers who perform essential functions unrelated to language. The case underscores the tension between linguistic identity and individual freedoms in India's federal structure.
items.title: Maharashtra's Marathi Language Rule for Taxi Drivers Sparks Constitutional Concern

key_points: SoftBank plans a $6.3 billion retail bond sale in Japan, the largest by any issuer, to fund OpenAI commitments and refinance debt.
The seven-year bonds will be priced on 4 September with a coupon range of 4.3-4.9%, marking SoftBank's third retail bond sale in 2026.
The move is part of SoftBank's strategy to secure funds for its AI investments, which include over $60 billion in commitments to OpenAI.
Analysts note the bond's reliance on retail investors due to banks' reluctance to take on the risk, with the deal likely to price toward the upper end of the coupon range.
SoftBank faces a $20 billion shortfall even after this issuance, suggesting potential offshore bond offerings, while S&P Global Ratings upgraded its outlook to stable.
items.summary: SoftBank Group plans to issue $6.3 billion in retail bonds in Japan, the largest such issuance by any issuer in the country, to fund its commitments to OpenAI and refinance maturing debt. The seven-year bonds, priced on 4 September with a coupon range of 4.3-4.9%, will be SoftBank's third retail bond sale in 2026. The move reflects the company's strategy to secure funds for its AI investments, which include over $60 billion in commitments to OpenAI. SoftBank's shares fell 5.3% following the announcement. Analysts note the bond's reliance on retail investors due to banks' reluctance to take on the risk. The company faces a $20 billion shortfall even after this issuance, suggesting potential offshore bond offerings. S&P Global Ratings upgraded SoftBank's outlook to stable, citing improved financial ratios.
items.title: SoftBank to issue $6.3 billion retail bonds for OpenAI funding and debt refinancing

key_points: ISRO transferred the complete SSLV to HAL for Rs 511 crore, marking the first time a space agency has handed over an entire launch vehicle to a company.
ISRO and HAL will collaborate during the initial two years as HAL builds its first two rockets, after which HAL will operate independently.
Critics argue that two years may not be enough for HAL to fully absorb the technology, citing past failures in transferring complex manufacturing knowledge.
A 2015 audit of HAL's Su-30MKI fighter production found limited indigenous content and higher costs, highlighting challenges in transferring critical design expertise.
The transfer is part of India's strategy to build a mature space economy worth $44 billion by 2033, with routine launches handled by industry.
items.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) transferred the entire Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) to Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) for Rs 511 crore, aiming to shift routine satellite launches to industry. ISRO will collaborate with HAL during the initial two years as it builds its first two rockets. Critics question whether two years is sufficient for HAL to absorb the technology, citing past failures in transferring complex manufacturing knowledge. A 2015 audit of HAL's Su-30MKI fighter production revealed limited indigenous content and higher costs, suggesting challenges in transferring critical design expertise. The deal marks a significant step toward India's goal of establishing a mature space economy worth $44 billion by 2033.
items.title: ISRO Transfers SSLV to HAL Amid Concerns Over Technology Absorption Timeline

key_points: Godrej Industries Group signed a MoU with Haryana's government for a ₹20,000 crore investment plan.
The investment aims to create around 40,000 jobs by FY28, building on existing ₹12,000 crore investment in the state.
Godrej Properties plans to invest ₹16,000 crore in real estate, with future projects expected to create over 11,000 jobs.
Godrej Ventures will invest ₹3,500 crore in Gurugram's Grade A+ office infrastructure, generating over 30,000 jobs.
items.summary: Godrej Industries Group signed a memorandum of understanding with the Haryana government, outlining a ₹20,000 crore investment plan to create around 40,000 jobs by FY28. The investment will expand on its existing ₹12,000 crore investment in the state, with Godrej Properties planning an additional ₹16,000 crore in real estate. Godrej Ventures aims to invest ₹3,500 crore in Gurugram's office infrastructure. The group highlighted Haryana's economic growth and urban development as key factors in its decision.
items.title: Godrej Industries to invest ₹20,000 crore in Haryana, aiming for 40,000 jobs by FY28

key_points: ISMA claims India has enough sugar stocks to meet demand and prices will drop.
Recent price rises are attributed to speculation and weather-related production issues.
Imports from Brazil may arrive before October 15, though the October 31 deadline is not strictly enforced.
NFCSF maintains production estimates despite industry revisions, expecting 15-20 lakh tonnes of sugar to be carried into November.
items.summary: The Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) asserts there is no sugar shortage in India, with sufficient stocks to meet demand. ISMA president Niraj Shirgaokar attributes recent price increases to speculative stocking and weather-related production issues. The government has allowed duty-free imports of up to 1 million tonnes of raw sugar to address rising prices. The National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories (NFCSF) maintains that domestic supplies are adequate, with production estimates for the 2025-26 season at 279 lakh tonnes. Imports from Brazil may arrive before October 15, though the October 31 deadline is not strictly enforced. The government is expected to consider shipments arriving after this date.
items.title: India's Sugar Supply Adequate, Prices Expected to Drop

key_points: Stock futures fell as rising Treasury yields and Iran tensions pressured markets.
Global bond yields, including the 30-year US Treasury yield above 5.3%, have increased borrowing costs and made bonds more attractive.
Investors fear prolonged US-Iran conflict could keep oil prices high, worsening inflation.
The US Treasury's measures to stabilize bond markets were short-lived and similar to quantitative easing.
Upcoming PCE inflation data and the Fed's Jackson Hole meeting will provide insights into interest rate policy.
items.summary: Stock futures declined on Monday amid concerns over rising Treasury yields and fears of prolonged US-Iran tensions. The Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq-100 futures all fell, following a week of market declines. Treasury yields, including the 30-year US Treasury yield reaching nearly 5.3%, have pressured stocks by making bonds more attractive and increasing borrowing costs. Global bond yields in Japan, France, and Germany also rose, adding to financial market concerns. Investors worry that a prolonged US-Iran conflict could keep oil prices high, exacerbating inflation. The US Treasury attempted to stabilize bond markets with measures similar to quantitative easing, but the effects were short-lived. The upcoming PCE inflation data and the Fed's Jackson Hole meeting will provide further clues about interest rates. Nvidia's earnings, expected to show potential price hikes for AI infrastructure, will also test market sentiment. Asian markets showed mixed performance, with Japan and South Korea experiencing declines. Overall, investors remain cautious due to a combination of higher yields, inflation worries, geopolitical risks, and major earnings reports.
items.title: Stock futures fall as Treasury yields and Iran tensions weigh on markets

key_points: A 31-year-old man in Kerala was arrested for sharing intimate videos of his wife and sexually abusing his daughter.
The wife discovered the videos after friends alerted her, leading to a police complaint.
The accused pushed for 'wife-swapping,' which the wife refused, and continued the alleged offences despite counselling.
The case is under investigation under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and POCSO Act.
The accused was traced and arrested after going into hiding.
items.summary: A 31-year-old man from Kerala was arrested for allegedly uploading intimate videos of his wife on a pornographic website and performing sexual acts in front of his four-year-old daughter. The wife discovered the videos after friends alerted her, leading to a police complaint. The accused also pushed for 'wife-swapping,' which the wife refused. Despite counselling, he continued the alleged offences, including another video of him engaging in sexual acts with the daughter. The case is under investigation under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and POCSO Act. The accused was traced and arrested after going into hiding.
items.title: Kerala man arrested for sharing intimate videos of wife and sexually abusing daughter

key_points: India's ethanol policy has shifted agricultural production, displacing traditional crops and raising food security concerns.
The policy's expansion of maize cultivation conflicts with NITI Aayog's goals for self-reliance in pulses and edible oils.
Ethanol production transfers public grain assets to private hands, generating revenue for distilleries while leaving farmers with uncertain prices.
The policy impacts consumers by reducing fuel efficiency and increasing feed costs for livestock, affecting millions of small vehicle owners.
The article advocates for equitable benefit distribution and suggests alternatives like crop residues for ethanol production, emphasizing the need for transparent policy adjustments.
items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: India's ethanol blending policy, which mandates E20 fuel, has significantly altered agricultural patterns by diverting foodgrains like maize and rice into biofuel production. This shift, driven by the Petroleum and Road Transport Ministries, has displaced traditional crops and raised concerns about food security. NITI Aayog reports highlight potential shortages in pulses and edible oils by 2047-48, yet the ethanol program continues to expand maize cultivation, creating a conflict with food self-reliance goals. The government's ethanol policy generates revenue for distilleries but transfers public assets to private hands, while maize farmers face uncertain prices and market instability. The policy also impacts consumers by reducing fuel efficiency and increasing feed costs for livestock. The article calls for a more equitable distribution of benefits and suggests alternatives like crop residues for ethanol production, emphasizing the need for transparent policy adjustments.
items.title: India's ethanol policy shifts food production, raises security concerns

key_points: The Maharashtra government's Marathi language requirement for drivers has caused service disruptions and higher fares in Mumbai.
Many elderly drivers, lacking formal education, struggle to meet the language requirement, leading to protests and strikes.
Critics argue the policy is impractical, with some suggesting it disproportionately affects working-class individuals.
Commuters report longer wait times and increased costs, with some opting for more expensive alternatives like taxis.
Advocates call for a more flexible approach, emphasizing the need for time and support rather than punitive measures.
items.summary: The Maharashtra government's new requirement for autorickshaw, taxi, and cab drivers to speak Marathi has led to increased fares and service disruptions in Mumbai. Drivers, many of whom are elderly and lack formal education, have protested the rule, with some staging strikes and blocking roads. Critics, including musician Avantika Ganguly and former actress Divya Unni, argue the policy is impractical and burdens hardworking individuals. Ganguly reported paying three times the usual fare and facing longer wait times, while Unni criticized the use of fines and harassment as methods to enforce language proficiency. Commuters have also expressed frustration, noting the disruption affects millions who rely on these services daily.
items.title: Mumbai commuters face higher fares and shortages due to Marathi language requirement for drivers

key_points: Apollo Micro Systems acquired a 34% stake in Shauryastra Defence Systems through a ₹34,000 cash investment.
Shauryastra Defence Systems was incorporated on 21 August 2026 to meet the Indian Armed Forces' advanced operational requirements.
The venture will be led by Dr V. K. Saraswat, with Apollo Micro Systems aiming to expand its defence electronics capabilities.
The acquisition aligns with the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative and strengthens Apollo Micro Systems' position as an end-to-end defence solutions provider.
Apollo Micro Systems also announced an open offer to acquire shares in Premier Explosives, with SEBI setting a 12-day tender period for the offer.
items.summary: Apollo Micro Systems has acquired a 34% stake in Shauryastra Defence Systems, a newly incorporated defence technology company. The investment involved a cash payment of ₹34,000 for 3,400 equity shares at ₹10 each. Shauryastra Defence Systems was established on 21 August 2026 to address futuristic operational needs of the Indian Armed Forces. The venture will be led by Dr V. K. Saraswat, with Apollo Micro Systems aiming to expand its defence electronics capabilities and align with the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. key_points: Saikat Majumdar critiques Avni Doshi's 'The First House' for its weak character development and narrative emptiness.
The novel's protagonist and husband are underdeveloped, with limited emotional depth and motivation.
Majumdar argues the characters fail to engage readers, despite Doshi's attempt to create a spectrum of unattractive figures.
The narrative is criticized for its vacuousness and claustrophobic tone, with the narrator's ruminations failing to evoke empathy.
The review highlights the novel's failure to transform the theme of marital decay into a compelling artistic experience.
items.summary: Saikat Majumdar's review of Avni Doshi's novel 'The First House' critiques the book's lack of compelling character development and narrative depth. While praising Doshi's choice to focus on marital decay without political polemic, Majumdar argues the characters remain elusive and emotionally irrelevant. The protagonist, a woman trapped in a failing marriage, is underdeveloped, with limited depth beyond her self-perceived unattractiveness and economic dependence. The husband is portrayed as a cardboard cut-out, and the daughters are passive, infantilized figures. Majumdar notes the novel's attempt to create a spectrum of unattractive characters fails to engage the reader, as they lack distinct personalities and emotional resonance. The narrative, set in a middle-class US suburb, is criticized for its vacuousness and claustrophobic tone, with the narrator's self-indulgent ruminations failing to evoke empathy. The review highlights the novel's failure to transform boredom into fascination, leaving a lasting impression of vague, half-baked expressions that fail to connect with readers.
items.title: Review of Avni Doshi's 'The First House' highlights weak character development and narrative emptiness

items.summary: The Delhi High Court has summoned right-wing commentator Abhijit Iyer-Mitra and media platforms The Pamphlet, Law Beat, and The Sunday Guardian over allegations of privacy violations by Saurav Das, a spokesperson for the Cockroach Janta Party. Das claims the defendants disclosed his home address and personal details online, leading to security risks. The court issued notices for an interim injunction and scheduled a hearing for September 14. Das seeks damages exceeding Rs 2 crore and permanent injunctions against the defendants. Legal arguments centered on privacy rights and the Puttaswamy judgment, with the court referencing a 1994 Supreme Court ruling on the matter.
items.title: Delhi High Court summons right-wing commentator and media outlets over privacy breach claims

items.summary: A video of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan leaving a hospital after a 2022 shooting attempt was shared as recent, but it is actually from November 2022. The footage shows Khan three days after being shot in the legs during a protest. A reverse image search and cross-referencing with reports from India.com and Agence France-Presse confirmed the video's origin. The claim is misleading as it falsely presents historical footage as current.
items.title: Video of Imran Khan Leaving Hospital After 2022 Shooting Misrepresented as Recent

key_points: The Petroleum Ministry has asked states to appoint district-level officers to accelerate the shift from LPG to PNG.
PNG is promoted as a safer, cleaner, and more efficient cooking fuel for India's energy transition.
The move follows disruptions in LPG supply chains during the West Asia crisis, highlighting the need for energy resilience.

items.summary: The Petroleum Ministry has directed states and union territories to appoint district-level nodal officers to expedite the transition of households from liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to piped natural gas (PNG). In a letter to state chief secretaries, Petroleum Secretary Neeraj Mittal emphasized that PNG offers a safer, cleaner, and more efficient cooking fuel, crucial for India's energy transition. The move follows disruptions in LPG supply chains during the West Asia crisis, which exposed India's reliance on Middle Eastern imports. Piped natural gas proved more resilient, prompting the government to expand city gas infrastructure. New regulations prohibit households from retaining both LPG and PNG connections, with district administrations tasked to support the transition by coordinating with gas distributors and resolving consumer issues.
items.title: Centre pushes States to speed up PNG adoption, seeks district-level officers to drive LPG-to-gas transition

items.summary: The Indian government has established maximum LPG production targets for 21 refineries and upstream companies, aiming to build a domestic supply buffer. The targets, set at 63,810 tonnes per day, exceed current domestic output and are intended to reduce reliance on imports. Reliance Industries is allocated the largest quota of 18,000 tonnes daily. The order mandates infrastructure upgrades and production measures to increase LPG output. The government can issue directives to refiners to ramp up production during supply disruptions. The framework follows emergency measures taken during the West Asia crisis to prevent future shortages.
items.title: Government sets LPG production targets for refineries to boost domestic supply
